# Engineering Log

## 2026-09-04: Paid provider spend is capped per prospecting run, not per batch

- `runProspectingBatch` accepts `maxVerifications`; `verifyCandidateEmails`
  computes the paid slots per company as `min(DEFAULT_VERIFIER_LIMIT, unique
  addresses)`, clamps them to the verifier calls still allowed in the batch,
  and counts the difference as `usage.verification.skippedByCap`. Every
  address still gets the deterministic checks. `DEFAULT_MAX_ENRICHMENTS` is
  exported for callers that combine it with a run budget.
- `context-prospecting.ts`: `stats.paidUsage` is added to the stored action
  (decoded as zeros for old payloads), `addPaidUsage` folds each batch's
  `usage.enrichment.calls` / `billable` and `usage.verification.calls` into
  it (also on the FAILED path when the batch itself returned), and
  `remainingPaidBudget` sets the per-batch caps before each
  `runProspectingBatch` call. The `runBatch` injection of
  `runCompanyContextProspectingAction` forwards both caps.
- Sales Agent card (`supply-os-context.tsx`): a "Paid lookups" row with usage
  against the budget, hidden while nothing paid was spent.
- Verification: `npx tsx scripts/leadgen.test.ts`,
  `npm run test:supply-os-context-prospecting`, `npx tsc --noEmit`,
  `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.

## 2026-09-04: Legacy re-keying must not move a row that is already keyed by its domain

- Post-merge review of #390: `persistCandidates` runs one `rekeyResearchRecords`
  and upsert pass per dedupe field, and when a batch held the same company
  with a domain and as a domainless directory line, the `company_name` pass
  matched the row the `domain` pass had just keyed (by its stored
  `company_name`), moved it onto the name key, and the name upsert replaced
  `data` with a row whose `domain` is null. The next domain-only run then found
  no row under the domain key and inserted a duplicate company.
- `rekeyResearchRecords` takes `keepKeyedBy`: a matched row whose current
  `dedupeKey` equals `normalizeDedupeValue(data[field])` for one of those
  fields is a current row, not a legacy one. Its target key goes into the new
  `keyedElsewhere` result, it is not written, and no other legacy row is moved
  onto that key either (the decision is made across the whole candidate set
  before any write, so it does not depend on row age). With `keepKeyedBy` the
  precedence check also covers targets whose key is already claimed, so a
  name-keyed duplicate left behind by the old behavior stops receiving
  name-only updates and the domain row stays the one that is fed; re-keying
  itself is still limited to free targets. Calls without the option are
  unchanged.
- `PROSPECTING_DEDUPE_FIELDS` fixes the precedence `domain` then
  `company_name`; `groupProspectingResearchRows` orders groups by it and
  `persistCandidates` passes the preceding fields as `keepKeyedBy`, then drops
  the inputs whose key came back in `keyedElsewhere` instead of upserting them
  (a domainless sighting carries less than the domain row already holds). Those
  candidates count as persisted because the company is in the list.
- Verification: `npm run test:research-lists` (new kept-row assertions),
  `npm run test:supply-os-context-prospecting` (real DB: mixed batch yields one
  domain-keyed row, later domain-only run updates it with the new email and
  keeps status; the same scenario failed before the fix with a spurious
  update), `npm run test:leadgen`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`;
  `npm run lint` reports only pre-existing findings outside this change.

## 2026-09-04: Repeated domains share one enrichment slot; legacy research rows move to the domain key

- Review of #389 found two gaps. First, directory documents are not
  domain-deduped (two chamber PDFs can list the same member), and every repeat
  spent a `maxEnrichments` slot before Hunter served its memo, so 40 repeats
  could starve later unique companies. `enrichCandidate` now keys its outcome
  by lowercased domain: repeats reuse the cached ranked contacts and the
  counters (`companiesEnriched`, `skippedByCap`) count unique domains.
- Second, rows written before company-keyed dedupe still carried an
  email-derived or null `dedupeKey`, and `upsertResearchRecords` matches only
  the stored key, so the next batch would have inserted a second row per
  company that could re-enter campaigns. `rekeyResearchRecords` runs before
  the domain-keyed upsert: it checks which stable keys are already taken in
  the office and list, then for the still-free ones looks up candidate records
  with a case-insensitive `string_contains` on `data[dedupeField]` (Postgres
  JSON filter, so `Lambda Steel GmbH` matches a batch spelled
  `LAMBDA STEEL GMBH`), confirms `normalizeDedupeValue(stored) === key` in
  code so a mere substring hit is skipped, and moves the oldest legacy
  row onto the stable key with a write conditioned on id, office, list and the
  previously read key. Later legacy rows for the same domain and rows whose
  stable key is already taken are left as they are (nothing is deleted or
  merged), a P2002 from a concurrent claimer is swallowed because the upsert
  will then update that row, and any other error propagates.
- Verification: `npm run test:leadgen`, `npm run test:research-lists`,
  `npm run test:supply-os-context-prospecting`, `npx tsc --noEmit` and
  `npm run build` pass; `npm run lint` reports only pre-existing findings
  outside this change.

## 2026-09-04: Leadgen gets a paid verifier and a named-contact enricher, both optional

- Prospecting found companies and role inboxes, but a campaign at 1,500
  sends/day needs deliverable, named decision makers. `verify.ts` now accepts a
  `MailboxVerifier` and `run.ts` a `ContactEnricher`; Bouncer and Hunter
  adapters live in `bouncer.ts` and `hunter.ts` behind `fetchImpl`, timeout and
  clock injection so every test runs against mocked transports.
- The heuristic verdict is computed first and is what survives whenever the
  provider cannot answer: no key, non-OK status, malformed JSON or payload,
  network error, abort on timeout, `unknown` status, or exhausted credits
  (Bouncer 402, Hunter 429). Exhaustion short-circuits later calls in the same
  run without counting them as failures; a failed Hunter lookup is dropped from
  the memo so a retry stays possible.
- Hunter runs only after discovery, only on candidates at or above the fit
  threshold, and at most `maxEnrichments` (40) times per batch. Generic
  addresses and records without a name are dropped, duplicates are ranked
  before dedupe so the stronger record survives, and enriched emails are merged
  with harvested ones and verified through the same path, so the paid verifier
  cap (6 per company) applies to both.
- `selectPrimaryContact` picks the row's email: best ranked named contact whose
  verification is not `undeliverable`, else the harvested public address, and
  no email at all when every address is known to bounce (the verdict still says
  `undeliverable`, so campaign audiences never inherit a bouncing address). The
  research row's `evidence_urls` include only the chosen contact's sources.
  `persist.ts` prefers the enriched name, title and phone and keeps both
  providers' metadata in `sourceRefs`.
- Review follow-ups: company research rows now dedupe on `domain` (falling back
  to `company_name`) instead of the shown email, because enrichment or a new
  verdict can change which address a company row shows and must update the
  same row rather than insert a second one. Directory rows with a domain go
  through the same `enrichCandidate` path as harvested sites (same fit
  threshold, cap and verification), while rows without a domain stay
  deterministic. `mailboxVerifierFromEnv()` and `contactEnricherFromEnv()`
  build a fresh adapter per call, so exhaustion, usage counters and memos are
  scoped to one `runProspectingBatch` instead of living in the process until
  the next deploy.
- Usage counters (`usage.verification`, `usage.enrichment` with companies
  enriched, with contacts, skipped by cap) are stored alongside `providerStats`
  on the run; `report.ts` ignores that key so provider summaries stay clean.
- Test isolation: both suites delete `BOUNCER_API_KEY` and `HUNTER_API_KEY`
  from `process.env` before importing, after a local run with real keys turned
  a heuristic MX assertion into a live undeliverable verdict.
- Verification: `npm run test:leadgen`,
  `npm run test:supply-os-context-prospecting`, `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
  `npm run lint` reports only pre-existing findings outside this change.

## 2026-09-06: A supplier conversation is now stored work, not a recomputed view

- Every earlier fix improved one step of the loop, but the state of a thread was
  recomputed each pass and nothing survived it, so a failed draft, a failed send
  or a quote that could not be written was reported once and forgotten, and that
  supplier stalled until somebody swept the request by hand.
- `ProcurementConversationTask` stores one row per office, request and supplier:
  the stage, the action owed, failed attempts, when it may be tried again, the
  last error and the last time it moved. `officeId, orderId, vendorId` is unique,
  so a pass updates a thread instead of adding to a queue, and a retry can never
  duplicate a supplier message on its own.
- `nextConversationTaskState` is pure and tested without a database. Attempts
  count failures only, so a thread waiting on its supplier stays due for the next
  pass at zero attempts, progress clears the count, and a failing thread backs
  off 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h then daily forever rather than being abandoned.
- Settled means a recorded quote. `NO_CONTACT_METHOD` is unreachable rather than
  settled, so a supplier with no address stays visible in the funnel without
  inflating the work the loop owes. `NEEDS_OPERATOR` stays owed, since nothing
  clears it on its own.
- Every thread the funnel covers is written back, not only the ones that failed,
  so a silent supplier stays owned. A failure overrides progress for the same
  supplier in the same pass, so a failed send is not masked by another phase
  touching that thread.
- The scheduled pass leads with the requests whose conversations are due, and
  keeps the rotation as the fallback, so a request that is behind is not starved
  and a request with nothing owed is not skipped forever. A due-task read is
  intersected with the queue the pass was already allowed to work.
- A store that refuses the write or the read no longer throws away a pass that
  already answered suppliers: it reports `backlog.stored: false` and
  `backlogReadFailed`, because an empty backlog and an unreadable store look
  identical otherwise.
- Contacted state now reads `last_email_message_id` or the legacy
  `gmail_message_id`, so suppliers reached by the bulk RFQ path are no longer
  projected as never contacted.
- Owning a request was not the same as owning a thread, so five leaks were
  closed on top of the first cut. A pass now honours each conversation's own
  backoff instead of retrying every thread of a request one of them made due. A
  thread the pass never worked, because a deadline or a batch limit stopped it,
  keeps its attempts, its error and its backoff instead of reading as a
  successful wait, which used to erase the retry history of exactly the threads
  that were behind. A supplier the request stopped pursuing is settled, so it
  cannot keep its request in the due queue forever. Due requests are grouped in
  the database and only then limited, so one request with a long tail of old
  threads cannot crowd out every other request. Scheduled eligibility reads the
  same current or legacy contacted stamp as the rest of the loop.
- The task table is on the `derya_app` allowlist in
  `scripts/sql/derya-app-role.sql`; the deployment boundary test in `prebuild`
  fails the build otherwise, which is how the missing grant surfaced.
- Verified with `npm run test:procurement-conversation-task`,
  `npm run test:procurement-conversation-stage`,
  `npm run test:procurement-conversation-task-db`,
  `npm run test:procurement-reply-send-db`,
  `npm run test:procurement-local-outreach-db`, the procurement autopilot, nudge,
  draft, quote, reply and attachment suites, `npx prisma validate`,
  `npm run db:generate`, `npm run lint` (no new errors in touched files;
  `src/lib/thread-actions.ts` and `src/lib/whatsapp.ts` keep their preexisting
  `no-explicit-any` errors) and `npx tsc --noEmit` (only the preexisting stale
  `.next/types/validator.ts` reference to a deleted campaigns page).

## 2026-09-05: Derya owns procurement order status

- Procurement workflow ownership defaults to Derya. `PROCUREMENT_WORKFLOW_OWNER=bourne`
  is the only opt-in for Bourne wake, retry, and reconciliation.
- Research mode follows the workflow owner when
  `PROCUREMENT_RESEARCH_MODE` is unset, so Derya research is enabled by
  default and explicit research mode values still override the fallback.
- The dashboard role advances only `researching`, `sourcing`, and
  `awaiting_order_approval` through the tenant-scoped, forward-only
  `advance_order_status` security-definer function. Its update compares
  ladder ranks against the current row, preserving concurrent forward
  progress. Operator-owned statuses such as `ordered`, `cancelled`, and
  `needs_attention` remain untouched.
- Supplier discovery, the first RFQ send, and the first recorded quote advance
  status through the shared helper. No send or approval behavior changed.
- Each sourcing, RFQ, and quote pass reconciles status from persisted supplier
  facts, so a failed status write can self-heal on a later pass with no new
  outcome.
- Campaign banner, request-derived ICP discovery, multiple contacts per
  company, and auto-reply loops are out of scope.


## 2026-09-06: A funnel that only counted repliers reported nothing owed

- The stage work reported the funnel from the reply scoped plan. A pass reads a
  conversation only for suppliers that answered, so on the PCBA request (359
  contacted, 22 replies) the funnel described 22 threads and a request whose
  every replier was quoted would have reported zero owed with 337 suppliers
  never followed up. The pass now stages the remaining vendors from the request
  projection it already loaded, minus the ones outreach is closed on, so the
  funnel counts the whole request without one extra thread read.
- Two smaller leaks from the same work: an out of office thread was allowed a
  third follow up, because the chase counter assumed the first message after an
  inbound reply was our answer, and a follow up that asked for a missing lead
  time then restated the whole commercial checklist, asking the supplier again
  for the price they had already given.

## 2026-09-05: Every fix moved one step, nothing owned the conversation

- After the discovery, attachment, ingestion, attribution, drafting, sending
  and quote reading fixes, requests still leaked: 66 real replies, one recorded
  quote, two partial readings sitting untouched, and threads whose only reply
  was an out of office notice never followed up. Each pass decided one action
  per thread and reported what failed, so a thread that received nothing looked
  the same as a finished one and only a manual sweep found it.
- A supplier thread now has a stage and a funnel, so a pass reports where its
  threads stand and how many still owe an action, and only a recorded quote
  counts as finished. The scheduled response carries the same counts, which is
  what removes the manual sweep from the loop.
- A partial reading is now a question, not a dead end. The quote sweep reports
  the missing fact, the plan asks the supplier for that fact on their own
  thread with the category files attached, and the scheduled pass delivers it,
  since waiting for an operator command is what left ubersmt (21 days, no
  price) and a molder (MOQ 100, 12 days, no price) short of a purchase order
  for a week.

## 2026-09-04: Add read-only outreach status ops action

- The authenticated campaign ops route now accepts `action: "status"` after
  resolving the office. It uses all campaign statuses by default and supports
  an optional `campaignId` filter without changing campaign state.
- `campaignRecipientFeedback` matches each office-scoped campaign's SENT
  recipients against current office suppressions and reports bounced,
  complained, opted-out, and other blocked recipients. Suppression counts can
  include suppressions created before the campaign.
- The database suite covers one campaign with a bounced and clean recipient,
  plus an empty campaign. The status action is read-only and does not add an
  approval or send path.

## 2026-09-04: Add a campaign reply digest and exclude delivery feedback

- Campaign summary reply grouping now applies the shared human-reply predicate,
  excluding deterministic bounces, complaints, opt-outs, and auto-replies that
  share the campaign thread, including unfinished feedback marked
  `DELIVERY_FEEDBACK` before `deliveryKind` persistence finishes.
- The shared human-reply predicate is null-safe, so unclassified inbound
  replies count as replies and suppress follow-ups.
- The read-only outreach ops `replies` action returns campaign counts for
  genuine replies and delivery feedback, plus a bounded newest-first digest of
  genuine reply threads. Answered state requires an outbound message strictly
  newer than the latest genuine inbound reply.

## 2026-09-04: A sweep blamed the thread mailbox for an unavailable sender

- The production sweep after the reply scope work answered every waiting reply
  it could and reported five as "that Gmail inbox is disconnected or disabled
  for sending", naming mailboxes the inbox diagnostic showed as active and
  ingesting. The pass allows the pooled sender, so the message was wrong about
  the cause: the pooled fallback had found no mailbox either, and the failure
  reported only the thread mailbox.
- The error now distinguishes the two blocks, and the read-only inbox diagnostic
  reports sender reach (pool size, mailboxes under their daily limit, remaining
  capacity, and the request's own mailboxes that cannot send), so an operator
  can tell a mailbox to resume from a pool with nothing left today.

## 2026-09-03: Answering replies outlasted the invocation limit

- A confirmed autopilot pass on a 424 supplier request returned 504
  FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT: `vendorStates`, `draftTargets`, and the send
  batch each walked every supplier row, reading a conversation (and, in the send
  batch, rereading the request) per row. The scheduled pass hit the same wall
  silently, so on any large campaign replies were never answered by the loop and
  only a small operator command could catch up.
- Every reply pass now scopes to `procurementRepliedVendors`, which overlays the
  office email records onto the projected response counts, so cost tracks
  replies received. The scheduled pass sends in best effort mode, stops at a
  240s budget while it can still report, and rotates the request queue by pass
  window.
- The same production pass also failed sends with "The selected Gmail sender is
  paused by sender protection.": the thread sender lookup accepted a paused
  mailbox, which the provider then refuses. Paused mailboxes are excluded from
  that lookup and the loop allows the pooled sender, so the answer leaves from a
  mailbox that can send instead of failing forever.
- Review found the send instruction was doing too much: one `autoSend` flag
  covered answers to current replies, quiet thread chases, and nudges to
  suppliers who never replied, so the scheduled pass would have mailed
  unsolicited follow ups nobody confirmed. Sending is split, the scheduled pass
  passes `sendFollowUps: false`, and it does not draft chases either, since a
  saved chase draft is indistinguishable from a ready reply draft to a later
  pass. Delivery is then restricted to threads whose newest message is the
  supplier's.
- Review then found the 240s budget only stopped the route from starting the
  next request, while one request runs a quote sweep, a draft batch, a thread
  scan per respondent and a send batch with no deadline of its own, so a slow
  request could still be killed at the function limit and discard the whole
  response. `runProcurementAutopilot` takes an absolute `deadlineAt`, checks it
  before every phase and between threads and chase drafts, and reports
  `stoppedAtDeadline`, which the route counts as deferred. Review then found two
  holes in that first guard: a phase that started in time could still outlast
  the deadline on its own, so the quote sweep stops between pages and the draft
  batch between drafts; and a scan that spent the whole budget left no time to
  send, so a request too large to scan in one pass would have answered nobody
  forever. Reading now stops a send reserve before the deadline and respondents
  rotate by window, so a partial scan sends what it collected and every thread
  is eventually read.
- Review then found two ways a reply could still never be answered. Respondent
  scope came from the capped presentation summary, so once an order passed
  1,000 mail records an older reply looked like no reply at all and its supplier
  was dropped from every pass; respondents now come from a paged read of the
  order's whole inbound history, scoped by office and request token, loading
  inbound mail plus the addresses we mailed on its threads and no other bodies,
  while the capped summary keeps serving the dashboard. And eight early draft
  targets that failed on every attempt held the whole batch, so later replies
  were never drafted; eligible targets now rotate by window like the queue, and
  a failed draft is reported in the pass failures instead of being counted and
  forgotten.
- Review then found the full history read could itself consume a scheduled
  invocation before a single reply was sent. The read now takes the caller's
  `outOfTime`, stops between pages, and returns `complete: false`, which the
  autopilot counts as `stoppedAtDeadline` so the request is deferred rather than
  reported as finished with fewer repliers than it has. Pages run newest mail
  first, so a read cut short still holds the replies waiting now, and the draft
  batch and quote sweep pass the same deadline through their own candidate
  selection.
- Two leftovers from that round followed. The pass named failed drafts but did
  not count them, so a pass whose every draft failed still reported zero
  failures; the count now covers the draft and chase draft paths too. And quote
  capture still chose its candidates from the capped presentation summary, so a
  priced reply older than an order's newest mail records was never read; it now
  takes the same full history reply scope the answer path uses, office and order
  scoped, with the read budget and cursor unchanged.
- Review also found that the mailbox filtering excluded the one mailbox that
  could settle an uncertain delivery: a paused sender left a RUNNING attempt
  unreconcilable, and the replacement sender changed the message hash, so the
  attempt was refused as a different reply. Reconciliation now uses the sender
  the attempt stored, including when no sender is available at all, and the
  guard compares what the supplier reads rather than the full hash.

## 2026-09-03: A protection pause between reservation and delivery no longer drops the recipient

- The Gmail send lookup refuses a mailbox whose `sendPausedAt` was set after
  the sender-pool reservation (`SENDER_PAUSED_ERROR`). Both campaign runners
  recorded that as a permanent `REJECTED`, so a reviewed recipient was lost to
  a bounce spike on a mailbox that would be resumed by an operator anyway.
- First touches (`runOutreachCampaignBatch`): the refusal now goes through
  `outreachCampaignPausedSenderAction`. In a rotated campaign the reservation
  is released and the loop repeats the same row, so `reserveEmailSender` runs
  again under the same idempotency key and request hash. The released
  reservation row is updated in place with the newly selected account, and
  `SHARED_SENDER_POOL_FILTER` (`sendPausedAt: null`) keeps the paused mailbox
  out of the selection, so the message leaves once from another ready mailbox.
  A recipient is rerouted at most once per run: a second pause, like any pause
  in a pinned campaign (operator-chosen mailbox), releases the claim as
  `POOL_EXHAUSTED` and stops the run, and the recipient is reclaimed later.
  Any other provider rejection still settles `REJECTED`.
- Follow-ups (`runOutreachCampaignFollowUps`): the step is never rerouted
  because the reply has to leave from the mailbox that owns the recipient's
  provider thread. `deferPaused` handles both a pause seen before the
  reservation and one returned by the provider after it: release the
  reservation and the claim, record a `POOL_EXHAUSTED` outcome, backfill the
  slot for rotated campaigns, stop the run for pinned ones. Before deferring it
  rechecks `threadReplied`, so a human reply that arrived while the mailbox was
  paused skips the step as `REPLIED` instead of parking it.
- Tests: rotated first touch paused on the first mailbox is re-reserved with the
  same key and sent from the second (one release, no `REJECTED`, no claim
  deletion); both mailboxes paused releases the claim without a third attempt;
  a pinned campaign never asks the pool for another account. Follow-up paused
  after reservation keeps the reservation pinned to the first-touch account,
  releases it once, and the recipient behind it on another mailbox still sends;
  a pinned follow-up run stops at the first pause with every claim released; a
  paused recipient whose thread gets a reply is skipped `REPLIED` on the next
  run.

## 2026-09-03: Alternate supplier senders could be read but not answered

- A confirmed autopilot pass failed 23 PCBA reply sends with "The supplier
  sender could not be verified for this thread." Thread attribution made those
  replies visible and quotable, but `requireQuietThread` and
  `requireCurrentInbound` still compared the newest inbound sender against
  `vendor.contact.email`, so every reply from a colleague or helpdesk address
  was refused at send time and the supplier kept getting chased instead of
  answered.
- The conversation, not the send path, decides who counts: the local RFQ
  conversation exports `attributedSenders` from the outbound recipients on its
  own thread, and both guards call `procurementSupplierSenderVouched`. Nothing
  operator supplied widens the set, an unattributed sender is still a conflict,
  and bounces never reach attribution.

## 2026-09-03: Follow-ups for rotated campaigns leave from the first-touch mailbox

- `runOutreachCampaignFollowUps` returned early when `senderAccountId` was
  null, which is exactly the shape sender rotation stores, so rotated campaigns
  stayed `ACTIVE` and never sent a follow-up. The runner now resolves each
  recipient's sender through `followUpSenderAccounts`: the pinned account for
  pinned campaigns, otherwise the connected `EmailAccount`
  (`SHARED_MAILBOX_POOL_FILTER`) whose email sent the first touch. Mailboxes
  are one app-wide pool, so the lookup is by email and not by the campaign's
  office. The reservation is pinned to that account so the reply stays in the
  recipient's provider thread. In a rotated campaign the step is settled per
  mailbox state: `sendPausedAt` set (sender protection, operator resumes)
  releases the claim and the run continues, as does a capacity refusal;
  disconnected or `sendEnabled = false` settles `REJECTED` without a
  reservation attempt. An address connected more than once is ranked READY,
  then PAUSED, then DISABLED regardless of row order, so a stale disabled row
  cannot turn a resumable step into `REJECTED`. A released rotated claim is refilled from the remaining
  due recipients whose mailbox has not refused in this run (each deferral
  blocks one more mailbox, so the chain is bounded by the number of distinct
  first-touch mailboxes, and every refill goes through `claimFollowUps` so the
  daily cap holds), so blocked mailboxes at the front of the plan cannot hold
  every slot on every run. Tests: two recipients on mailboxes from two offices reserve their own
  account, one exhausted mailbox defers one recipient while the other sends
  with its original `providerThreadId`; missing, disconnected, and disabled
  mailboxes yield `REJECTED`, a paused mailbox releases its claim; with
  `limit: 1` an exhausted or paused mailbox at the front still lets the ready
  recipient behind it send; a duplicated address that is disabled in one row
  and paused in another waits in both row orders.

## 2026-09-03 - Replies from an address we never mailed

- Recovering a reply by thread was not enough: attribution to a supplier still
  compared the sender address against the supplier's recorded contact, so a
  reply from `mluna@mfg-one.com` to an RFQ sent to that shop's sales address
  answered for nobody. In production this hid genuine answers from MFG One,
  Summit Interconnect, Dallas Foam, Witmold, and Attractive Plastics: no
  response counted, the vendor conversation stayed empty, quote reading never
  saw the message, and the follow up loop kept the supplier on the chase list.
- `summarizeLocalRfqOutreach` and `localRfqConversationFor` now build the
  addresses we mailed per thread and attribute an inbound message to the ones
  sharing the sender's domain, falling back to the single address mailed on that
  thread. A thread mailed to several unrelated addresses attributes nothing,
  because the reply could belong to any of them, and the sender address stays in
  the responded set so a supplier row recorded under it keeps matching. The
  response count keys on the mailed addresses, so one shop writing from two
  addresses is one response.
- Our own addresses are the account emails plus the sender of every outbound
  message, because a pooled mailbox can have no account row and its synced sent
  copy would otherwise read as the supplier answering with our own text.
- A delivery notice is excluded from attribution and from the response count:
  treating a bounce as an answer would both invent a response and suppress the
  follow up the failed delivery should trigger. Bounce wording is decided by
  `supplierBounceText`, exported from inbound triage. Wording only a mail system
  writes ("Mail delivery subsystem", "Undeliverable") counts anywhere, while
  generic wording ("Delivery failure", "Address not found") counts only in the
  subject or at the head of a body line, so a supplier writing "delivery failed
  inspections are re-worked at our cost" stays a real answer. The batched
  outreach query carries the first 2000 characters of each body so a service
  that states the failure only in the body is still caught.
- Attribution is thread scoped, so it cannot reach across requests or offices,
  and a recovered message keeps its stored direction rather than being inferred
  from the sender.
- `scripts/procurement-local-outreach.test.ts` covers the colleague reply, the
  forwarder, the ambiguous multi recipient thread, the provider bounce with
  body-only evidence, an outbound copy with no account row, and the daemon
  bounce; `scripts/procurement-local-outreach-database.test.ts` proves the same
  against a migrated database including the vendor conversation.

## 2026-09-03: Feedback is not a reply, refused reservations settle the claim, cc in the DSN fallback

- Follow-up reply detection matched inbound rows with `deliveryKind = null`,
  which is also the state of stored delivery feedback whose persistence is
  still being retried. `repliedThreadIds` now uses `humanReplyMessageFilter`
  (`NOT classification = DELIVERY_FEEDBACK` on top of the null check). Tests:
  unfinished transient bounce plus auto-reply in the thread still sends the
  step; finished feedback next to a real reply still skips as `REPLIED`.
- A refused sender reservation other than pool capacity deleted the follow-up
  claim (and left the first-touch claim `QUEUED`), so a `DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN`
  refusal caused by an orphaned `RESERVED` reservation was retried every reclaim
  window with no path to reconciliation. `settleOutreachReservationFailure`
  (shared by both runners) keeps the release for `POOL_EXHAUSTED`/`POOL_EMPTY`,
  records `UNKNOWN` linked to the open reservation for `DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN`,
  and records `REJECTED` otherwise. Tests: an orphaned reservation under the
  follow-up key yields one `UNKNOWN` row that the next run reconciles to `SENT`
  at the reservation time (or `REJECTED` after NOT_FOUND past the window); an
  `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` yields a `REJECTED` row that is never reclaimed; the
  first-touch runner upserts `UNKNOWN` with the reservation id and settles only
  its own `QUEUED` claim as `REJECTED`.
- `threadOutboundRecipients` selected only `toEmails`, so a DSN naming no
  recipient for a message with a cc'd address attributed and suppressed only
  the To recipient. It now returns To plus Cc. Test: mixed To/Cc fallback
  suppresses both.

## 2026-09-03: Suppressed rows leave the run budget, nudge late recheck, live outstanding count

- First touches: `selectOutreachCampaignSnapshotRows` sliced the audience to
  the run limit before `rejectSuppressedCampaignRows` ran, so a suppressed row
  inside the slice cost a slot and left daily capacity unused. The snapshot
  selection no longer takes a limit; `selectSendableCampaignRows` walks the
  unhandled audience in run-sized chunks, records suppressed rows as `REJECTED`
  as it passes them, and stops at `limit` sendable rows. Test: cap 2 with two
  suppressed rows interleaved still sends two and rejects both.
- Supplier nudges: the recheck added in the previous pass ran before
  `reserveEmailSender`, so a suppression landing during the reservation still
  reached the provider. The recheck now runs after the reservation (past the
  `completed` short-circuit) and releases the reservation on a hit; the source
  contract in `scripts/procurement-supplier-nudge.test.ts` pins that order.
- Follow-ups: `runOutreachCampaignFollowUps` returned `plan.outstanding` from
  before the sends, so the run that delivered a final step still reported it
  outstanding. The count is re-read through `outstandingCampaignFollowUps`
  after the loop. Assertions: the step 1 run reports 1, the final step run
  reports 0, the late-bounce run reports only the sent sequence.

## 2026-09-03: Suppression rechecked at the provider boundary, per-recipient DSN permanence

- Late suppression: campaign first touches and follow-ups planned from one
  suppression snapshot and then sent sequentially, so a bounce, complaint, or
  opt-out synced mid-run still reached the provider. Both runners, and the bulk
  RFQ runner, now call `listSuppressedEmails(officeId, [recipient])` after the
  sender reservation and before `provider.send`. A hit releases that
  reservation and settles only this run's `QUEUED` claim: `REJECTED` for first
  touches, `SKIPPED` (`BOUNCED` or `SUPPRESSED`) for follow-ups, `BLOCKED` for
  bulk RFQs, each with `suppressionSkipMessage`. The bulk RFQ check moved from
  before the reservation to after it so the reservation window is covered too.
  Tests: stateful fakes where the provider call for the first recipient records
  a suppression for the second; the second never reaches the provider and its
  reservation is released. Bulk RFQ source contract updated to the new order.
- Per-recipient permanence: `bouncePermanence` read one `Status:` for the whole
  message, so a mixed report suppressed the 4.x.x recipient too. `parseBounce`
  now splits the DSN into recipient blocks (blank lines, or each
  `Original-Recipient`/further `Final-Recipient` field) and decides each block
  on its own Status, Diagnostic-Code, SMTP code, then wording. Permanent
  recipients go to `recipients`, transient ones to the new optional
  `transientRecipients`, encoded after a `|` in the stored recipient list; rows
  stored before this decode unchanged. Header-listed and failure-line
  recipients keep the message-level verdict.
- Evidence order: numeric codes now outrank wording and transient wording
  outranks permanent wording, so "451 4.7.1 Recipient address rejected:
  Greylisted" is transient. Fixtures: greylisted rejection, mixed 5.x.x/4.x.x
  report with and without blank lines, persistence of the mixed report
  suppressing only the dead address.
- `isComplaint` accepted `Feedback-Type: not-spam`, and the `feedback-report`
  content type matched before the type was read. The type is read first and
  `not-spam` returns no feedback at all.
- `isOptOut` matched opt-out wording in the inherited `Re:` subject. Subjects
  now count only without a reply or forward prefix and at 80 characters or
  less; otherwise only the unquoted body is read. Fixtures: interested reply
  under a `Re:`/`FW:` subject carrying opt-out copy is not an opt-out; a bare
  "Unsubscribe" subject still is.

## 2026-09-03: Deterministic procurement campaign convergence

- Added pure campaign classification, bounded operator overrides, stored-plan
  validation, and convergence helpers.
- Sourcing command jobs now read good-lead and quote progress, cap each slice
  to the remaining target, and record why a campaign stopped before queueing
  another slice.

## 2026-09-03 - Research projects group prospect lists

- Added office-scoped research projects with optional list assignment and
  project-aware list APIs.
- Context prospecting drafts now name their workflow, and named projects are
  reused when runs create or attach research lists.
- Supply OS Prospects selects a project before a list, supports creating
  projects, and removes the direct record import panel.
- Verified with Prisma validation and the research and Context prospecting
  contract suites.

## 2026-09-03 - Preserve list tails in project collisions

- Project collision slugs now hash the full project and list identity, preserving
  deterministic separation for long list slugs.

## 2026-09-03: Context prospecting fit gate

- Context prospecting now persists only tier A/B candidates (fit >= 50), matching the leadgen persist gate.

## 2026-09-03: Outreach sender rotation and office recipient dedupe

- Campaign plans can rotate across enabled shared-pool mailboxes and report
  the available pool capacity, while reservations continue enforcing
  per-account caps.
- Planning first keeps one row per normalized address within a campaign, then
  excludes recipients contacted by another campaign in the office. Claiming
  repeats both filters inside a transaction. `SENT`, `QUEUED`, and `UNKNOWN`
  block later contact, while `REJECTED` does not. A `QUEUED` row blocks only
  while its campaign is not cancelled and the claim is within the reclaim
  window. Cancellation releases queued claims, and completion treats
  recipients blocked by another live claim as resolved. Human approval is
  unchanged. A successful sender reservation marks a queued row in flight
  before the provider call, so cancellation releases only unreserved queued
  rows. Provider rejection releases the sender reservation and records a
  non-blocking `REJECTED` row.
- Serializable claim conflicts are retried once on `P2034`, then treated as an
  empty claim if the retry conflicts again.
- Activation keeps the approved audience snapshot to avoid rerunning
  office-wide dedupe, while send-time status checks and personalization hashing
  continue to protect delivery.

## 2026-09-03: Attach approved follow-ups to active campaigns

- The ops campaign route now passes `followUps` through campaign planning and
  exposes a `followups` action for existing campaigns.
- The action requires an active ADMIN in the resolved office and the exact
  confirmation phrase `approve outreach follow-ups`. It normalizes and
  validates each step before writing.
- `setCampaignFollowUps` recomputes the revision hash from the stored campaign
  content and approved audience snapshot plus the new steps, then changes only
  `followUps` and `revisionHash` for DRAFT, ACTIVE, or PAUSED campaigns.
- Follow-up sequences are positional in the existing ledger, so replacement is
  rejected once any follow-up row has been queued or sent. Sequence versioning
  was intentionally not added.
- The route rejects malformed arrays before normalization, while omitted
  plan-time follow-ups remain optional.
- Completion now compares the loaded revision hash in its final ACTIVE to
  COMPLETED update. If follow-ups or another approved change commit between
  the completion snapshot and that update, the compare-and-set fails and the
  next batch reevaluates the campaign.
- Completed and cancelled campaigns are refused. First-touch copy, sender,
  audience, personalization, variants, and daily cap remain pinned.
- Verified with the outreach copy, send, and planning database suites, product
  copy checks, Prisma validation and generation, TypeScript, targeted lint, and
  diff checks.

## 2026-09-03 - Supplier replies that lost the RFQ reference

- Request level reply matching read only messages whose subject still contained
  `[RFQ xxxxxxxx]`, so a supplier answering through a helpdesk, or a client that
  rewrote the subject, left an answer that belonged to no request. Production
  diagnostics found 41 such inbound messages across the two HypnoDreamz
  requests.
- `loadLocalRfqMessages` now also reads inbound messages on the threads the
  request's tagged messages already occupy, and `localRfqOutreachByOrder`
  claims them for the request that owns the thread. A subject that still
  carries any reference is left to the request that owns that reference, and a
  null subject counts as carrying none.
- References are read case insensitively, so a client that recases
  `[RFQ xxxxxxxx]` still resolves to the request that owns it, and a thread
  carrying two requests' references anchors neither of them because an untagged
  reply on it could answer either.
- Recovered messages flow through the existing conversation, triage, and quote
  reading paths unchanged, so a bounce stays a bounce and only supplier
  authored price plus lead time still records a quote.
- `scripts/procurement-local-outreach-database.test.ts` proves the recovery,
  the office boundary, and that another request's tagged reply is not stolen,
  against a migrated database in the supplier reply delivery CI step.

## 2026-09-02: Production migration workflow accepts automated dispatch

- The protected production migration workflow now accepts
  `repository_dispatch` events with type `production-database-migration` and
  a `client_payload` of `{ migration_id, confirmation }`.
- Manual and automated triggers share the Production environment, exact
  confirmation phrase, latest-committed-migration check, pinned database
  identity checks, and committed verification SQL.

## 2026-09-02: Batch approval with spot checks

- Problem: approving hundreds of sends card by card is the throughput ceiling
  once contacts are good, but approving "the first ten rows" as a proxy for the
  audience hides what the other rows get and gives a reviewer no way to strike
  a bad recipient without re-planning from scratch.
- `src/lib/batch-review.ts`: `spotCheckSample` keeps the first 3 rows and
  picks 7 more at seeded positions spread across the remainder (SHA-256 of
  seed and slot), so a 250-row audience shows the head, the middle, and the
  tail, and the same revision always shows the same rows.
  `summarizeRecipientQuality` counts repeated domains, role mailboxes, free
  mail, duplicates, and invalid syntax and emits advisory warnings only.
- Outreach: `planOutreachCampaign` renders subject and body for each sampled
  row and returns `audienceQuality`; the `START_OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN` proposal's
  review items are the spot check, labelled with position and kind, and the
  proposal detail states approval covers all eligible rows. `exclude_emails`
  travels inside `filters` so it is already part of `campaignRevisionHash`,
  the saved draft, and activation's stale-plan rejection. Tool result trims
  rendered bodies out of the model-visible payload.
- Procurement: `listBulkRfqTargets` takes the resolved file package and
  returns `batchHash` from `bulkRfqBatchHash(order, sendable, files)`:
  `batchRecipientHash` (vendor id and normalized address), per target the
  subject and the body exactly as the send renders it (sorted by vendor id),
  and filename, content type, and SHA-256 of every attachment. Review found
  that a recipient-only hash would let a changed specification, a renamed
  vendor (greeting), or a swapped drawing go out under an old approval, and
  that a preview loader failure silently reviewed an RFQ without files. The
  admin preview now fails with 503 when the package cannot be loaded, takes
  `limit` and
  `excludeVendorIds`, and returns a `batch` block with the hash, a spot check
  with rendered RFQ bodies, quality lines, and the exact POST body.
  `runProcurementBulkRfq` accepts `excludeVendorIds` and `expectedBatchHash`,
  resolves the files before the check, and throws `BulkRfqBatchChangedError`
  after selection and before `reserveEmailSender` when the hash differs; the
  route maps it to 409. Existing callers without a hash are unchanged.
- Tests: `scripts/batch-review.test.ts` (bounded, deterministic, no repeated
  positions, head and spot labels, quality counts and warnings, hash
  properties, exclusion eligibility, exclusion changes the revision hash and
  no exclusion keeps it stable); `procurement-bulk-rfq.test.ts` source
  contracts updated for the exclusion argument, the file load before the hash
  check, and the 503 preview, plus hash cases for changed copy, changed
  vendor name, and changed attachment bytes under the same name.
  `batch-review.test.ts` also pins that `plan_outreach_campaign` puts
  `plan.revisionHash` on the proposal and returns a tool error when the saved
  draft's revision differs from the planned one (list edited between plan and
  save), so the approval always derives from the reviewed snapshot. Added to
  `supply-os-tests.yml`.
- Review follow-up: global outreach proposals have no job or inquiry page, so
  the decision queue sent them to the inbox where `reviewItems` were never
  rendered, and chat `apply <id>` could activate a campaign whose spot check
  nobody had opened. `src/lib/outreach-proposal-review.ts` lists pending
  office-scoped `OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN_START` proposals and splits each stored
  detail into subject and body; `supply-os-outreach-approvals.tsx` renders a
  Pending approvals panel in the Outreach desk (action details, every
  spot-check email in full with a Read checkbox, then Discard and Start
  campaign). `outreach-approval-actions.ts` recomputes unread items from the
  stored proposal server-side and refuses the apply while any remain, then
  reuses `applyPendingJobAgentProposal`; `agent-chat.ts` answers `apply <id>`
  and the greenlight phrase with a redirect to the panel when the target is an
  outreach proposal. Procurement `excludeVendorIds` are lowercased at the
  route and inside `listUncontactedBulkRfqTargets`, and rows compare
  case-insensitively, so an uppercase uuid no longer slips past a strike.
  Contracts in `batch-review.test.ts` (parser, chat gate ordering, server-side
  unread check before apply, content before the Start control, disabled until
  all read) and `procurement-bulk-rfq.test.ts`.
- Third review pass on the same surface. Legacy proposals: pending proposals
  saved before spot checks were rendered carry only "Eligible research-list
  row." details, and the parser accepted them, so the checkbox surface could
  have started a campaign with no message shown. The parser now sets a
  `blocker` when any surviving item lacks a `Subject:` line or when there are
  no items; the panel renders the reason with Discard only and the server
  action refuses the apply. Scope: the list was office wide while the apply
  went through `proposalWhere` with the caller's `userId`, so a colleague's
  card always answered "no longer pending". `ApplyJobProposalInput` gained
  `officeWide`, set only by the outreach action; the chat redirect and
  greenlight count dropped their `userId` filter to match. Roles: the actions
  accepted any non-EMPLOYEE operator, so a SALES account could call them
  directly and activate a campaign. Start and Discard now require ADMIN or
  MANAGER (the `canApproveProcurement` roles); SALES still plans campaigns and
  sees the pending list read-only with the reason in the footer. Contracts
  extended in `batch-review.test.ts`.
- Fourth review pass. Atomicity: the outreach apply activated the campaign
  first and marked the proposal `APPLIED` afterwards, and the discard updated
  by id without a status predicate, so a concurrent Start and Discard could
  leave a discarded proposal with an active campaign. The apply now claims the
  proposal with `updateMany({ status: "PENDING" } -> "APPLYING")` before
  `activateCampaign`; a zero-count claim returns "no longer pending" with no
  side effect, a blocked or throwing activation releases the claim back to
  `PENDING`, and the final `APPLIED` write only matches `PENDING`/`APPLYING`.
  `discardPendingAgentProposal` is a compare-and-set from `PENDING` and returns
  null when it loses. Kind boundary: the outreach Discard called the generic
  helper by id only, so an approver on the Outreach desk could discard a job,
  inquiry, or inbox proposal in the office. Both helpers accept `kind`, and the
  outreach actions pass `OUTREACH_PROPOSAL_KIND`. Role freshness: the actions
  read `session.role` from the long-lived cookie, so a demoted or deactivated
  user kept approval rights until the cookie expired. `resolveOutreachReviewer`
  loads the current `User` row (`officeId`, `isActive`) like the Supply OS page
  does and derives `canView`/`canApprove` from the stored role. Contracts in
  `batch-review.test.ts`.
- Fifth review pass. Status precondition: `activateCampaign` validated the
  revision and blockers but never checked the campaign status, so approving a
  still-pending proposal could restart a campaign that had been cancelled in
  the meantime. `campaignStatusBlocker` (outreach-campaign-copy) refuses any
  status other than `DRAFT` before audience work, and the activation write is
  now `updateMany({ status: "DRAFT" } -> ACTIVE)` that stamps `approvedAt` and
  `startedAt` in the same write; a zero-count result reports the current
  status as a blocker, so a cancel racing the approval wins. Stale claims: a
  proposal claimed `APPLYING` stayed there forever if the process died before
  the final `APPLIED` write, and disappeared from the pending list.
  `reconcileStaleOutreachClaims` runs at the start of
  `listPendingOutreachProposals` (so list, apply, and discard all see the
  settled state): for each outreach proposal in `APPLYING` older than
  `STALE_OUTREACH_CLAIM_MS` (5 minutes) it loads the campaign by office; a
  campaign with `approvedAt` was activated, so the proposal is finalized as
  `APPLIED` with the reviewer recorded at claim time, otherwise activation
  never completed and the claim is released to `PENDING`. Both writes are
  compare-and-set on `APPLYING`. Behavioral test with a fake db plus source
  contracts in `batch-review.test.ts`.
- Sixth review pass (own PR after #355 merged). Claim ownership: stale
  recovery matched on `status: APPLYING` alone, so a release could hand the
  proposal to a discard or a second Start while the original activation was
  still paused, and that activation then wrote `ACTIVE` anyway. A claim is
  now `{ proposalId, officeId, claimedAt }` (`claimOutreachProposal`,
  `releaseOutreachClaim`, `finalizeOutreachClaim` in
  `outreach-proposal-review.ts`); release and finalize match the exact
  `reviewedAt` written at claim time, which recovery nulls and a new claim
  replaces. `activateCampaign` takes `finalize(tx)` and runs the
  `DRAFT -> ACTIVE` write and the proposal finalize in one
  `prisma.$transaction`; a finalize that finds the claim gone throws
  `ClaimLostError`, the campaign write rolls back, and the apply reports
  `CAMPAIGN_CLAIM_LOST_BLOCKER`. The generic post-action `APPLIED` write is
  skipped for `START_OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN`. Existence leak: chat `apply <id>`
  queried office-wide pending outreach proposals before checking access, so a
  customer, EMPLOYEE, or stale session could learn whether an approval was
  pending. `resolveOutreachReviewer` (shared with the approval actions) runs
  first; only a live viewer is matched office wide, everyone else only against
  proposals they own, and the greenlight count is gated the same way. Panel:
  a failed initial load was hidden because `canView` started false;
  `loadError` is tracked separately and rendered even before access is known,
  cleared by the next successful load. Fake-db race test (claim, stale
  release, refused late finalize and release, second claim, discard) plus
  source contracts in `batch-review.test.ts`.
- Recovery follow-up (own PR after #357 merged). `reconcileStaleOutreachClaims`
  still settled rows on `status: APPLYING` alone, so a reconciler that
  selected a stale row and wrote late (after another reconciler released it
  and a reviewer re-claimed it) cleared the fresh claim. It now selects
  `reviewedAt` and settles through `ownedClaimWhere`, the same predicate as
  release and finalize. Fake-db test with a reconciler paused between select
  and write while the row is released and re-claimed.

## 2026-09-02: Delivery feedback, second review pass

- Encoding: `encodeStoredDeliveryFeedback` sliced the whole serialized value to
  500 characters, so a long recipient list could remove the `: ` delimiter and
  leave a row that recovery could never decode. The header is now built within
  the budget (recipients appended whole while they fit, `-` when none fit) and
  only the detail is cut. Test: 40 long recipients round-trip to a prefix of the
  real list; one 600-character address is omitted rather than truncated.
- Attribution: `resolveUnroutedFeedbackOffices` only looked at `toEmails`, so a
  bounce for a cc'd address on an IMAP-synced outbound message had no origin
  and created no suppression. The prefilter and the exact parsed-address check
  now include `ccEmails`.
- Late suppression: the nudge and bulk RFQ runners planned once and then
  reserved senders from that snapshot, so a suppression persisted between
  planning and sending was mailed anyway. Both loops now recheck
  `listSuppressedEmails(officeId, [recipient])` immediately before
  `reserveEmailSender` and record a deterministic skip or `BLOCKED` outcome.
  Planning-time suppression stays, so the run limit still counts only sendable
  rows. Source contracts in both test scripts.

## 2026-09-02: Delivery feedback review fixes

- Retry: sync stored `deliveryKind` together with the message, so a failure in
  event, suppression, or sender pause left a message that looked finished and
  was never revisited. The message row no longer sets `deliveryKind`;
  `recordDeliveryFeedback` sets it last. `deliveryFeedbackNeedsRecovery`
  (`classification = DELIVERY_FEEDBACK`, `deliveryKind = null`) is checked in
  the existing-message branch of `gmail-sync.ts` and `imap-sync.ts`, which
  re-parse the provider message and call `recordDeliveryFeedback` on the stored
  message and thread. Failures are still caught per message.
- Durable recovery: the existing-message branch only sees provider messages
  inside the sync window (IMAP: `lastSyncAt` minus ten minutes), and
  `lastSyncAt` advances even when persistence failed, so a row could stay
  unfinished forever. Both syncs now store the parsed feedback in
  `classificationReason` (`encodeStoredDeliveryFeedback` /
  `decodeStoredDeliveryFeedback`, `KIND permanent|transient a@x,b@y: detail`)
  and finish with `recoverUnfinishedDeliveryFeedback`, a bounded query on
  stored `DELIVERY_FEEDBACK` rows with `deliveryKind = null` that decodes the
  stored feedback (falling back to re-parsing the stored body), routes by the
  stored thread's office or `UNROUTED_MAIL_THREAD_MARKER`, and calls
  `recordDeliveryFeedback` per row with per-row error isolation. No schema
  change; the sweep is idempotent because the event upsert is keyed by message.
  The batch orders by `classificationAt` (nulls first) and stamps every row
  that does not finish with the attempt time, so undecodable rows or rows
  whose persistence keeps failing rotate to the back instead of occupying the
  50-row window on every sync while newer feedback waits.
- Routing: an unthreaded report used to be recorded and suppressed on the
  connecting office. `recordDeliveryFeedback` now takes `routing`; for
  unrouted reports `resolveUnroutedFeedbackOffices` reads the mailbox's
  outbound history for the affected addresses. One office: attribute there.
  Otherwise: event on the fallback office, no suppression. Sender protection is
  unchanged.
- Limits: `runProcurementBulkRfq` selected `limit` raw rows, then dropped
  suppressed ones, so a run could send nothing while eligible suppliers waited.
  `listUncontactedBulkRfqTargets` loads all eligible rows,
  `selectBulkRfqBatch` partitions by suppression and caps only the sendable
  side (`boundedBulkRfqLimit`). `listSupplierNudgeTargets` now loads the
  suppression list itself and skips suppressed rows before they count toward
  `limit`; the runner sends `planned.targets` as is. The admin preview used to
  cap raw rows before suppression, so a send could reach suppliers past the
  reviewed list once suppressed rows filled the preview; `listBulkRfqTargets`
  now returns the same `{ sendable, blocked }` batch the run computes and the
  preview reports `blocked` separately.
- Parser: `bouncePermanence` checks `Status:` first, then transient patterns,
  then the generic Failure subject, so a mailbox-full or 4.x.x diagnostic under
  a Failure subject is transient. ARF recipient fields accept `rfc822;`.
- Tests: failure injection with recovery for each persistence step, shared
  mailbox unique/ambiguous/unknown origin, generic-failure transient and
  permanent fixtures, `rfc822;` fixture, bulk RFQ starvation regression, and
  updated nudge and sync source contracts.

## 2026-09-02: Bounce and complaint feedback loop

- Scaling outbound volume with no bounce handling burns sending domains, and
  the synced inboxes already receive every DSN and complaint. The loop reuses
  that sync instead of adding provider webhooks.
- `src/lib/email-delivery-feedback.ts` is a pure parser: DSN detection by
  `report-type=delivery-status`, mailer-daemon senders, and failure subjects;
  permanence from the `Status:` code or Gmail's "address couldn't be found"
  copy; ARF complaints by `report-type=feedback-report` or `Feedback-Type:`;
  auto-replies by `Auto-Submitted`, `X-Autoreply`, and subject prefixes;
  opt-outs by short unquoted phrases only, so our own footer quoted back in a
  reply never counts. Affected recipients come from `Final-Recipient`,
  `Original-Recipient`, `Original-Rcpt-To`, `Removal-Recipient`, or the failure
  line, with the mailbox's own address removed.
- `src/lib/email-delivery-events.ts`: `recordDeliveryFeedback` upserts one
  `EmailDeliveryEvent` keyed by message id (repeat syncs are no-ops), falls
  back to the thread's last outbound recipients when a DSN names nobody,
  upserts `EmailSuppression` on `(officeId, email)`, and runs
  `applySenderProtection` for bounces and complaints. `listSuppressedEmails`
  normalizes addresses and maps unknown stored reasons to `MANUAL`.
- Outbound checks sit before sender reservation in
  `outreach-campaign-send.ts` (`rejectSuppressedCampaignRows`, ledger row
  `REJECTED`, no daily-cap slot), `outreach-campaign-follow-ups.ts` (persisted
  suppressions merged into the planner sets), `procurement-bulk-rfq.ts`
  (`partitionSuppressedRfqTargets`, outcome `BLOCKED`), and
  `procurement-supplier-nudge.ts` (skipped with the deterministic reason).
- `SHARED_SENDER_POOL_FILTER` adds `sendPausedAt: null`; the mailbox filter
  used by inbound sync is unchanged.
- Fixed while testing: the parser returned no recipients for auto-replies
  because the sender address was filtered as "own".
- Tests: `scripts/email-delivery-feedback.test.ts` (new, in the supply-os
  workflow) plus suppression scenarios in the send, follow-up, bulk RFQ, and

## 2026-09-02: Outreach campaigns gain follow-up sequences

- Campaigns were single touch. `OutreachCampaign.followUps` now stores up to
  three normalized steps, and the new `OutreachCampaignFollowUp` table is the
  per-recipient ledger keyed by `(campaignId, recordId, step)` so a claim can be
  taken once under concurrent cron runs.
- `runOutreachCampaignFollowUps` reuses the campaign send path: sender-pool
  reservation with a per-step idempotency key, pause recheck before every send,
  the shared campaign daily cap, local thread and message recording, unknown
  send reconciliation, and rejected-send release.
- Only `SENT` rows advance a sequence. Rejected and unknown rows end it, replies
  detected through inbound messages on the linked local thread skip it with
  reason `REPLIED`, and a `suppressedRecipients` set skips with `SUPPRESSED`
  or `BOUNCED` so the bounce feedback loop can plug in without changing the
  planner.
- `completeCampaignIfDone` waits for outstanding sequences, so the cron keeps
  picking the campaign up after first touches are exhausted.
- Tests: `scripts/outreach-campaign-copy.test.ts` covers normalization,
  blockers, subject defaults, timing, and planner ordering.
  `scripts/outreach-campaign-follow-ups.test.ts` runs the sender against a
  stateful fake database for threading, step progression, reply and
  suppression skips, pause, shared daily cap, run limit, idempotency, rejected
  and unknown outcomes, and stale claim reclaim.
- Review hardening: first-touch and follow-up claims now take a per-campaign
  advisory lock (`lockOutreachCampaignClaims`) and compute one shared remaining
  capacity from `SENT` rows today plus every live `QUEUED` claim in both ledgers
  (`outreachCampaignRemainingCapacity`). `input.limit` is a total per-run budget:
  follow-ups receive `limit - firstTouchClaims`. Each follow-up rechecks the
  local thread for an inbound reply immediately before the provider call and
  skips with `REPLIED` after releasing the reservation. Early exits (pause, pool
  exhaustion) release every unprocessed claim in the batch. Campaigns cannot
  complete while an `UNKNOWN` row in either ledger still holds a `RESERVED`
  reservation; reconciliation confirms `SENT` or, after `NOT_FOUND` for 24
  hours, releases the reservation and records `REJECTED`.
- Merge with main's A/B variants: the plan's spot check and the activation
  blockers take `variants`, and the activation write inside the claim
  transaction uses `campaignActivationTransitionWhere` (DRAFT plus the reviewed
  `revisionHash`) instead of a status-only predicate. Because variant
  assignment is keyed by campaign id, `planOutreachCampaign` reports
  `spotCheckCampaignId` and `plan_outreach_campaign` re-plans once against the
  saved draft when they differ, and follow-ups derive their `Re:` subject from
  the recipient's variant (`followUpInitialSubject`). The send test's paging
  fixture gained the advisory-lock and follow-up ledger stubs the shared claim
  transaction needs.
- Third review pass. An `UNKNOWN` send that reconciliation later confirms is
  recorded with the reservation's `createdAt` as `sentAt` (both ledgers), so the
  next follow-up step is due from the original delivery, not from the cron run
  that recovered it. The first-touch loop tracks its position in the claimed
  batch and `releaseClaimsFrom(index)` deletes the remaining `QUEUED` rows of
  this campaign when the campaign pauses or the sender pool empties; before, a
  paused batch kept its capacity for 30 minutes and blocked follow-ups.
  `gmailSendAccount` and the app-password send lookup now refuse a mailbox
  whose `sendPausedAt` is set right before delivery (`SENDER_PAUSED_ERROR`),
  mapped to `REJECTED` without `needsReauth`; the reconcile lookup is
  unchanged so a paused mailbox can still confirm earlier sends. Tests: the
  follow-up suite asserts a recovered step keeps `sentAt` and step 2's `dueAt`
  from the reservation time; the send suite covers pool exhaustion and a pause
  mid-batch releasing exactly the unattempted claims; the provider suite covers
  a paused sender never reaching Gmail while reconcile still works.

## 2026-09-02 - Operator login throttling, daily code cap, generic errors

- Unsolicited sign-in codes reached the founder mailbox because the only limit
  was 3 codes per 15 minutes per email and nothing limited the sender.
- Extracted `consumeLoginAttempt` into `src/lib/login-throttle.ts` from the
  customer portal limiter, which now delegates to it with the same identity and
  therefore the same stored key hashes. No schema change: the shared counter
  keeps using `CustomerPortalLoginThrottle`.
- The operator login server actions consume `login-code:`, `login-verify:`, and
  `login-password:` budgets per client address before touching the database.
  The password form previously accepted unlimited guesses against customer
  office usernames.
- `requestLoginCode` takes the client address for logging and rejects a mailbox
  that has already received 12 codes in 24 hours.
- Review follow-up: address budgets are best effort because `x-forwarded-for`
  is caller controlled, so the address now comes from `x-vercel-forwarded-for`
  first and failed password guesses additionally consume a per-identifier
  budget (`loginAttemptsExhausted` reads it, only failures spend it). The
  throttled copy no longer promises a 15 minute wait it cannot honour for the
  daily cap, and submitted identifiers are kept out of the logs unless already
  known to be an operator mailbox.
- Review follow-up: `POST /api/auth/session` guessed passwords behind a
  module-level `Map`, which resets per serverless instance, so it now consumes
  the same persistent budgets through injected `consumePersistentAttempt` and
  `persistentAttemptsExhausted`. The budgets and identity builders moved to
  `src/lib/auth-session-route.ts`, which the login form imports, so the two
  password surfaces cannot drift apart. The in-memory counter stays as a cheap
  first check.
- Review follow-up: the counted mailbox caps read persisted codes, which are
  written only after delivery, so concurrent requests could each pass both
  counts and each send mail. `requestLoginCode` now consumes an atomic
  `login-code-send:<email>` budget of one per 30 seconds immediately before
  sending, which serializes a mailbox and makes the counts hold under a burst.
- Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `tsx scripts/login-code.test.ts`,
  `tsx scripts/customer-portal.test.ts`, `tsx scripts/auth-session-route.test.ts`,
  `npm run check:product-copy`. Touched-file lint reports only the pre-existing
  `no-html-link-for-pages` error on the portal link in the login page.

## 2026-09-02: Quote write tenant boundary and per message provenance

- The shared `dashboard_api` role lost its update privilege on `order_vendors`.
  Quotes are recorded by executing `record_order_vendor_quote`, a security
  definer function with a fixed search path that writes the quote column only,
  requires the order to belong to the calling customer, refuses an empty quote,
  and refuses a row that already holds a quote. The migrated database test
  proves a direct update is denied, a foreign customer's call changes nothing,
  the owning customer's call lands, and a second call is refused.
- `mergeSupplierQuoteThread` records the message each fact came from and the
  evidence each contributing reply supplied, and the capture path stores both,
  so provenance survives a merge across replies.
- A refusal binds its own clause, so a refused amount is not read as a price
  while a replacement price elsewhere in the sentence still is.
- Labelled unit and total cues run through the same ancillary charge filter as
  bare amounts, so a tooling total or a per unit freight charge is not a price.
- An adversative turn is read for direction: a refusal before an amount refuses
  that amount, a refusal after one takes it back, and a new amount after a
  refusal is a counter offer. So "we cannot meet $10 but we can do $12.50"
  records $12.50, "$10 per unit, but we cannot commit to that price" records
  nothing, and "but we cannot cover freight" leaves the price standing.
- A withdrawal now binds inside its own message too: facts stated before it are
  cleared and the withdrawal sentence itself is not read, so "unit price $7.50,
  lead time 12 days. That quotation is withdrawn" records nothing while a
  replacement stated after the withdrawal still records.
- A refusal reaches back through the thread merge, not only through its own
  reading: the amounts a newer reply refuses may not be restored from an older
  reply, and a supplier refusing their own price with no replacement leaves no
  older price standing, while a refusal about freight or another term leaves it
  alone and a price stated with the refusal still records.
- A reply subject counts as supplier evidence only when the supplier wrote it.
  The capture passes the outbound subjects of the thread into the reading, and a
  heading matching one of them once reply prefixes are stripped is our own RFQ
  line quoted back, so an RFQ naming a target price cannot complete a reply that
  states nothing but a lead time. A heading the supplier rewrote is read for
  facts, and a subject of unknown provenance is treated as ours.
- A question about our target binds its own clause, so "your budget of $4.50 is
  below our cost, our price is $6.20 per unit" records $6.20, while a disclaimer
  such as "indicative only" or "ballpark" governs every amount in its sentence
  whatever clause each one sits in.
- Quote capture runs before the autopilot plan, so a supplier whose newest
  reply carries a quote is read as quoted in the same pass and is neither
  chased nor answered.
- Repeated separators of one kind are grouping, since a number holds a single
  decimal point, so "$1,234,567" and "EUR 1.234.567" both read as the million
  they name instead of being dropped.
- Candidate selection overlays the office email records on the projected
  response count, because a reply this app delivered may never appear in the
  workflow ledger. Without it a locally synced priced reply was never read.
- A later statement inside one reply supersedes the earlier one, the same rule
  the thread merge applies across replies, so "unit price $7.50 ... correction:
  unit price $7.80" records $7.80 for price, total, quantity, MOQ, and lead
  time alike.
- Three digits after a single separator are thousands only when the integer
  part is one to three digits and does not lead with a zero, so "$0.125" and
  "EUR 0,125" read as fractions of a unit while "$1,240" still reads whole.
- A write that failed no longer sits behind the page cursor:
  `quoteCursorBeforeFailures` stops the returned cursor before the earliest
  failed supplier, so a database outage costs a retry and not a lost quote.

## 2026-09-02: Quote capture hardening

- Quote writes go through the workflow role, so the role contract now grants
  `UPDATE (quote, updated_at) ON order_vendors` to `dashboard_api` and keeps
  every other column denied. A migrated database test proves the first write
  lands, a second is refused by the no-overwrite predicate, and an update of
  unrelated columns is denied.
- Commercial facts are matched inside their own clause, so a nearby freight,
  setup, tax, or warranty amount cannot pass as a price and a validity or
  payment period cannot pass as a lead time.
- A withdrawal or expiry in a newer message ends the merge instead of falling
  back to the price it retracted.
- Respondents are paged by vendor id with a returned cursor, so consecutive
  bounded passes cover every reply rather than the same first forty.

## 2026-08-31: Supplier quote capture

- A supplier reply is read into commercial facts deterministically, with the
  supplier sentence kept as evidence, so a recorded price is auditable and no
  model invents one.
- A purchase order needs a price and a date, so only a reading holding both is
  recorded. A price with no lead time, a lead time with no price, a budget
  question, a ballpark, and a disclaimed figure are reported and left alone.
- The write targets only supplier rows holding no quote, so a rerun records
  nothing twice and an operator recorded quote survives.
- The capture reads conversations only for suppliers that answered, which keeps
  a request of several hundred silent suppliers inside the route budget.

## 2026-09-02: Outreach campaigns page through the whole audience

- `runOutreachCampaignBatch` sliced the audience to `dailyCap` rows before
  excluding records that already had a ledger row, so every run after the
  first day re-read the same first rows, found them all handled, and claimed
  nothing. Campaigns larger than one day's cap stalled at `dailyCap` sends.
- The batch now loads the campaign's ledger record ids first and excludes them
  before the slice, so day two pages into the next unsent rows. The locked
  claim still re-checks the ledger, so concurrent runs stay idempotent.
- `scripts/outreach-campaign-send.test.ts` runs a three-day, cap-one campaign
  against an in-memory ledger and asserts one distinct recipient per day.

## 2026-09-02 - Serper-first leadgen search cascade

- The cascading lead search now uses Serper first whenever a key is
  configured. It only calls free HTML engines when Serper returns fewer than
  the deduplicated threshold, preserving combined page budgets and provider
  call-order accounting. Without a key, the free-only cascade is unchanged.

## 2026-09-02: Harden activation races and imported email fields

- The final outreach activation transition is conditional on the
  office-scoped campaign remaining in `DRAFT`, so cancellation during
  approval work cannot be overwritten.
- Planning now resolves address keys such as `primary_email` when imported
  fields are typed as `text`, and both callers pass optional list-shape
  inputs through.
- Activation also compares the approved revision hash, while draft saves use
  a conditional transition and create a fresh draft if activation wins first.
- Email-field inference now accepts only address-shaped final segments, avoiding
  metadata keys such as `email_verdict` and `email_confidence`.
- Explicit campaign names are also suffix-resolved when a fallback draft must
  be created after activation wins a save race.

## 2026-09-02 - Office Mail revalidates operator access

- Office Mail rejects customer sessions before querying the database, then
  re-reads the active user by id and office before either thread listing or
  detail access. Fresh role and whole-office access control the result, so
  deactivated users and restricted SALES users cannot read message bodies.
- The Supply OS page passes the same whole-office flag to the client shell and
  only restores the Mail tab for whole-office operators, ADMINs, or MANAGERs.

## 2026-09-02: Reject activation of closed outreach campaigns

- Activation now requires `DRAFT` status before any approval work. Cancelled
  and completed campaigns return a status-specific blocker, while pause and
  resume continue using their existing transitions.
- The final activation transition is also conditional on the office-scoped
  campaign remaining in `DRAFT`, preventing a concurrent cancellation from
  being overwritten.

## 2026-09-02: Campaign variants and authenticated ops sending

- Added validated campaign variants with deterministic campaign and record
  assignment, persisted `variantKey` values, and aggregate banner metrics.
- Added the authenticated ops campaign route for mailbox discovery, planning,
  approval, and capped runs. Approval records a real ADMIN user, requires

  against a fresh local PostgreSQL database using the committed read-only SQL
