## 2026-09-02: Context research runs continue server-side

- Context prospecting actions now opt into durable continuation when an operator
  starts them. A five-minute cron tick claims eligible office-scoped actions,
  runs bounded batches, retries failures, and stops at the row target or the
  end of the query plan.
- The browser chain remains as a fast feedback path while the tab is open.
  Background work writes reviewable research rows only and never sends
  outreach.

## 2026-09-02: Prospecting signal precision

- Metal-domain detection now matches normalized word tokens by exact match or
  prefix, preventing terms such as `core` and `forestry` from matching `ore`.
- Exact metal markers no longer treat ordinary words such as `Oregon`,
  `ironing`, or `acoustic` as metal domains. Plural exact markers are handled
  without broadening the deliberate linguistic stems.
- Narrow compound stems preserve metal-domain detection for ferromanganese,
  steelmaking, and ironworks without restoring broad `iron` or `ore` prefixes.
- Non-metal drafts require derived product or segment evidence; generic
  business, audience, and geography wording is excluded from that evidence,
  and generic industrial terms are only a fallback when no derived tokens
  exist.

## 2026-09-02: Unknown follow up deliveries reconcile, and eligibility is rechecked at send time

- Suppressing later rounds while a follow up is unconfirmed parked that supplier
  forever, because `reconcileProcurementBulkRfq` only settles first sends.
  `reconcileProcurementSupplierNudges` settles `procurement-rfq-nudge:`
  reservations: it rebuilds the round's RFC message id, asks the provider,
  records a confirmed send on the original thread, releases a send the mailbox
  never saw, and leaves anything still uncertain reserved. Every run reconciles
  before it reads the plan, and `POST { action: "reconcile" }` runs it alone
  without a confirmation phrase because it mails nobody.
- The plan is read once and the run then mails one supplier at a time, so a
  request cancelled or a supplier ruled out mid run could still be contacted.
  Eligibility is now re-read immediately before each reservation, and a target
  that closed in the meantime is skipped with that reason. The same recheck
  counts inbound messages on the thread, so a supplier that answers mid run is
  never sent the obsolete follow up that was already planned for it.
- Reconcile only touches slots whose last attempt is older than
  `NUDGE_RECONCILE_MIN_AGE_MS`, because releasing a slot that still belongs to a
  send in flight would let a concurrent run mail the same supplier twice. The age
  is read from `updatedAt`, so a reservation the pool reuses for a retry is
  protected exactly like a first attempt. A pass is capped at ten reservations
  and stops at its own 90 second budget, since one provider check can spend its
  whole timeout and the route allows 300 seconds. A slot still uncertain after a
  check is touched and the batch is ordered by least recently checked, so stuck
  deliveries rotate instead of holding every pass and starving newer ones, and a
  pass with nothing old enough to check still reports every unresolved slot.

## 2026-09-02: Supplier follow up eligibility narrowed after review

- A dry run without an explicit limit planned one supplier while a send defaults
  to the whole run, so the plan an operator approved could cover fewer recipients
  than the send. An absent limit now means the whole run.
- A follow up whose delivery came back unknown stays reserved. It used to count
  as a spent round, so the next run could mail the same supplier again before the
  first was resolved. A supplier with an unconfirmed follow up is now skipped
  with that reason until reconciliation decides.
- An ordered or cancelled request now contacts nobody, and a supplier whose
  status ended outreach (rejected, declined, excluded, disqualified, archived) is
  no longer eligible. The plan reports a closed request through `blocked` so an
  empty plan is not read as every supplier having answered.
- Autopilot counted only draft send failures in `failed`, so a pass where every
  follow up failed reported zero. Both paths now feed one total.

## 2026-08-31: Suppliers that never replied now get a follow up

- Diagnostics on the two live HypnoDreamz requests showed 261 suppliers past the
  quiet threshold with zero follow ups ever sent. The chase path builds a reply
  from the supplier's newest inbound message, so a supplier that never answered
  the first RFQ had no anchor and was skipped without a recorded reason.
- `src/lib/procurement-supplier-nudge.ts` follows up on our own RFQ instead: the
  same local thread, the same mailbox that owns the thread, `In-Reply-To` on the
  RFQ message id, and the same category scoped request files the RFQ carried.
  Eligibility lives in `src/lib/procurement-supplier-nudge-policy.ts`: no quote,
  no inbound reply, a recorded first send, quiet for four days, at most two
  follow ups per supplier.
- Idempotency follows the bulk RFQ pattern. Each round reserves
  `procurement-rfq-nudge:<orderId>:<round>:<vendorId>` from the sender pool, a
  completed reservation reports `ALREADY_SENT` without mailing anyone, a rejected
  send releases the slot, and an unknown one stays reserved for reconciliation.
- `POST /api/admin/procurement-supplier-nudges` needs the confirmation phrase to
  send; `GET` returns the plan with a skip reason per supplier. The autopilot
  pass reports `nudgeCandidates` always and only sends when the operator turned
  sending on.
- Verification: `npm run test:procurement-supplier-nudge`,
  `test:procurement-autopilot-plan`, `test:procurement-bulk-rfq`, `next lint`,
  `npx tsc --noEmit`.

## 2026-09-01: Context prospecting targets and multilingual fit

- Context prospecting profiles now derive deterministic fit signals from the
  approved product focus and segments, combining normalized multilingual
  industrial terms with the existing non-industrial exclusions.
- Removed broad multilingual tokens that caused substring false positives and
  replaced them with more specific metallurgy terms. Added regression coverage
  to keep hotel pages in the reject tier.
- The multilingual vocabulary is now selected only when the approved draft
  contains a metal-domain marker. Other drafts use product-neutral industrial
  terms, with regression coverage for packaging versus steel pages.
- Prospecting batches allow up to 60 queries and 300 page fetches within the
  existing 240-second budget. Drafts normalize a row target from 50 to 5,000,
  defaulting legacy drafts to 500. The Context panel counts unique created
  rows, continues completed batches until that target, and cancels stale loops
  when the workspace changes.
- Background continuation now pages past terminal actions, retires exhausted
  and permanently failed payloads, and caps each scan at 500 rows. Claim
  tokens prevent stale workers from overwriting newer progress, while inactive
  or missing action creators lose background authority. Action progress commits
  before LeadGen bookkeeping, so tail bookkeeping failures do not lose rows or
  query offsets.

  carries them into every thread.
- The context agent's structured reply gained a required `memoryNotes` array.
  The prompt instructs the model to return only new or changed durable
  company-level facts (and always when the operator explicitly asks to
  remember something), never chat-specific task details. Returned notes are
  citation-stripped and persisted after the reply.
- New route `POST/DELETE .../context/memory` and a Memory tab in the chat
  drawer let operators save and remove notes directly. Notes created by
  operators are not customer visible (standard `companyContextActorData`).
- Verified: `scripts/supply-os-context.test.ts`,
  `scripts/company-context-database.test.ts` additions (persistence, dedupe,
  agent packet, deletion, foreign-office rejection),
  `scripts/product-copy-policy.test.ts`, typecheck, build.

## 2026-09-01: Outreach recipient pinning and runtime grants

- Added migration `20260901000300_outreach_campaign_pinning` and paired
  production verification for per-recipient personalization storage. Runtime
  grants come from `20260901000200_leadgen_outreach_app_grants`.
- Activation captures the exact email, company, and country values used for
  each approved row. Batch selection skips rows without a pinned snapshot or
  later-ineligible statuses and renders from pinned values rather than current
  research data. The approved audience can shrink but never grow.
- Empty or unreadable active audience snapshots return `NO_AUDIENCE` without
  completing the campaign.
- Personalization now participates in the stale-approval revision hash.
  Every attempted batch records `lastRunAt`, which the campaign banner labels
  as the last attempt. `apply <id>` gates only outreach campaign proposals for
  customer and employee sessions, using the same office and user scope as
  proposal application.

## 2026-09-01: Outreach campaign hardening

- Added read-only production verification for the outreach campaign migration,
  including table, index, constraint, foreign key, and `derya_app` privilege
  assertions.
- Campaign completion now leaves preclaimed `QUEUED` rows outstanding until a
  terminal delivery status is recorded.
- Approval proposals show the full rendered body and eligible audience count,
  with the first ten recipients retained as review items.
- Greenlight now requires an operator session and a pending proposal owned by
  the current office and user. Cron uses nulls-first `lastRunAt` ordering, and
  run-now validates finite integer limits against the campaign daily cap.

## 2026-09-01: Outreach approval integrity

- Campaign drafts now persist a revision hash and eligible audience id
  snapshot. Applying a stale proposal refuses activation, and later batches
  use the approved snapshot rather than expanding to newly imported rows.
- Batch claims reserve campaign daily capacity transactionally, reclaim stale
  queued claims after 30 minutes, recheck campaign status before each send,
  and reconcile uncertain provider deliveries before selecting new rows.

## 2026-09-01: Outreach campaign chat controls and dashboard banner

- Added sender-mailbox discovery, office-scoped research-list and campaign
  tools, deterministic planning, and direct pause, resume, cancel, and run-now
  controls. A clear plan creates the existing pending proposal shape only when
  no blockers remain.
- Added the `START_OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN` proposal apply branch and greenlight
  command. Applying activates only; sends remain in the campaign batch runner.
- Added the active campaign banner and server actions. Summaries use stored
  audience totals and aggregate send and reply counts, with a safe empty
  fallback while the migration is pending.

## 2026-08-31: Prospecting failed on missing lead gen tables

- A read-only query against the production database showed 38 of 41 committed
  migrations applied, with `LeadGenRun` and `LeadDiscovery` absent, which is why
  Run research returned `Supply OS request failed.` The route caught a Prisma
  P2021 and had no branch for it.
- The workflow rejects anything but the latest migration directory on main, so
  the fix is a new tail migration rather than a verification file for an older
  one. `20260901000200_leadgen_outreach_app_grants` grants `derya_app` select,
  insert, update, and delete on `LeadGenRun`, `LeadDiscovery`,
  `OutreachCampaign`, and `OutreachCampaignSend`, since Prisma creates tables
  as the owner with no grants and the workflow never reruns the role script.
  This follows `20260825000200_research_lists_app_grants`.
- Its verification script asserts the five pending migrations are recorded,
  both lead gen tables exist with their tenant and run constraints,
  `LeadDiscovery.usableContact` is non null without a default, and `derya_app`
  has exactly the expected privileges on the four tables, then reports run,
  discovery, orphan, cross office, and outreach counts.
- `supplyErrorResponse` maps P2021 and P2022 to 503 with a migration message and
  logs otherwise unhandled failures, so an environment behind on schema is
  diagnosable from the response and the logs.
- Chat message citations no longer render. `documentCitations` filters the
  rendered chips to the `document:` prefix, so an answer or an action card still
  names the uploaded file it drew on, while "Operator message" style chips are
  gone in favour of the message bubbles that already show authorship. Stored
  citations are untouched.
## 2026-08-31: Sourcing state, panel alerts, and a quieter Supply OS shell

- The customer sourcing panel now names its own state instead of showing a bare
  `Start requested` control: not started, start requested with the local request
  time, researching, blocked, awaiting approval, or ordered. The five stages
  (request received, sourcing start, supplier search, supplier outreach,
  evidence review) print the concrete numbers behind them (quantity, needed by,
  owning worker, supplier names, contacted, replies, quotes, unqualified
  candidates) so an operator can see what the system did, not just that it ran.
- Sidebar alerts: `src/lib/supply-os/panel-alerts.ts` derives a chat alert from
  the newest agent message plus open clarifying questions and pending suggested
  actions, and a sourcing alert from request updates ranked blocked, approval
  ready, supplier replies, then generic updates. `use-supply-os-panel-alerts.ts`
  polls the sourcing list and the new
  `GET .../context/activity` route every 30s and stores per browser seen
  timestamps in `localStorage`. No notification tables, no schema change.
- Facility state is actionable. The shell header shows the verified operating
  base when logistics has one and otherwise a button that opens Logistics to set
  or verify it, so a research derived location is never presented as verified.
- Visual cleanup toward `DESIGN.md`: the company avatar chip is gone, the chat
  drawer header no longer overlaps at narrow widths (no wrap tabs, fixed size
  close button, truncating title), radii were pulled back to the 8/10/12 scale,
  and IBM Plex Mono was removed from procurement metadata labels.
- Browser testing of this pass found two gaps, both fixed here: the numeric
  stage lines were unreachable because the five stage list only rendered in the
  `researching` phase, which requires zero supplier candidates, so the list now
  also renders (compact) in the compare and procure phases; and a wake that
  failed (503 with no workflow webhook) still read as `Start requested`, so a
  failed start is now its own state (`Start request failed`) carrying the API
  message in a `startError` that the 7s status poll cannot clear.
- The empty chat renders four starter prompt cards that either prefill the
  composer or submit through the existing `submitMessage` path. Visible Context
  copy is now Chat.

## 2026-08-31: Context intake handles relative dates, citation tokens, and multi-question answers

- `normalizeContextProcurementDraft` no longer rejects a whole draft over an
  invalid `neededBy`: any value that is not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date becomes
  null. The agent prompt now carries the current date in the packet as `today`
  and instructs the model to convert relative timing like "within 8 weeks" to
  a concrete date or leave `neededBy` null with the wording in notes. Found by
  recorded browser testing where relative timing caused a retryable 503.
- Visible agent answers are passed through `stripCitationTokens`, which removes
  raw `[document:...]` and `[message:...]` tokens the model sometimes writes
  into the answer text. Structured `citationIds` provenance is unchanged.
- Clarifying-question chips now select instead of submit. Answers accumulate
  per question on the latest agent message and a single "Send answers" button
  submits them together, so answering one question no longer skips the rest of
  the round. Selections reset when a new agent message arrives or the thread
  changes.
- Verification: context and context-procurement contract tests, product copy
  policy, `npx tsc --noEmit`.
## 2026-08-31: A coverage number for the stale action guard

- Context: the guards existed (`scopeHash`, immutable task input, gate
  revalidation, draft revisions) but nobody could say which action paths block
  on state that moved, or how often the guard refuses work it should allow.
- Added `scripts/state-recheck.test.ts` and the `test:state-recheck` script. It
  drives real persistence functions on a local database, advances the process
  clock past a specific validity window, and classifies each run as a detected
  stale execution, an escaped stale execution, or a false conflict.
- Two scenarios were written wrong before they were written right, and both
  taught something. Rewriting a frozen approval input to fake staleness is not
  reachable in production because the database refuses it, so that case became a
  tamper assertion instead. Recording a quote release with an old release date is
  legitimate when qualification was valid on that date, so the release scenario
  now records the release on the day the guard runs.
- Result on 2026-08-31, 6 repeats per scenario: 114/114 stale executions
  detected, 0 escaped, 0/36 false conflicts, p50 15 to 17ms and p95 26 to 32ms on
  a local database.
- Verification: `npm run test:state-recheck`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`
  (only pre-existing findings in unrelated files).
## 2026-08-31: Context chat works for offices without a procurement mapping

- `chatWithCompanyContext` resolved the procurement customer id synchronously
  while building the `queueSourcingCommandFromChat` arguments, so an office
  absent from `PROCUREMENT_CUSTOMER_MAP_JSON` threw before the surrounding
  `.catch` and every chat request returned a raw 500. The customer id is now
  resolved separately; unmapped offices skip the deterministic sourcing-command
  path and chat normally. Found by recorded browser testing.
- Verification: context and context-procurement contract tests,
  `npx tsc --noEmit`.

## 2026-08-31: Context load filters messages by the selected thread

- `loadCompanyContext` accepts an optional `threadId` and applies the same
  database-side thread predicate as the agent path (shared
  `companyContextThreadWhere`, `Prisma.AnyNull` for General), and both context
  GET routes read a `?thread=` query param (`general` for the null thread).
  The UI requests the active thread and refetches on thread switch, so a
  less-active chat no longer appears empty once 500 newer messages belong to
  other chats.

## 2026-08-31: Context chat review fixes (history bounds, fail-open duplicates, thread limit status)

- `loadCompanyContext` and `assembleCompanyContextForAgent` now run separate
  bounded queries per kind (threads, documents, messages) with newest-first
  message pagination, so mature workspaces no longer lose recent threads or
  the newest turns of the active chat behind a single ascending `take`.
- The agent's `openRequests` duplicate-protection summary no longer swallows
  read failures into an empty list; a failed read fails the chat request
  instead of silently disabling duplicate detection.
- Thread creation routes map `CompanyContextLimitError` to a 429 with the
  limit message instead of a generic 500.
- The context contract test now pins the new drawer label
  `Ongoing requests and files` (the old `Files in context` copy was replaced
  by the request drawer redesign), which fixes the `database-contracts` CI
  failure on the previous merge.
- Verification: context test suite, context-documents, supplier-email
  provider tests, `npx tsc --noEmit`, lint clean on changed files.

## 2026-08-31: A sourcing wave starved its second category

- Production symptom: across nine drains of the 100 per category wave, molded
  foam grew from 126 to 136 suppliers while PCBA stayed frozen at 181, and the
  queue payload only ever carried a `molded-foam` search cursor.
- Cause: a slice hands the whole budget to one category because a discovery call
  needs room to answer, and a later category that no longer fits is left to the
  continuation slice. The continuation rebuilt the same plan order, so the first
  category took the budget again and the second one never ran.
- Fix: `runSourcingCommand` reports the categories it could not reach as
  `skipped` and accepts `firstCategory`, which rotates the plan. The queued job
  hands the next slice the starved category and keeps the chain alive while any
  category is still owed a turn, so the two categories alternate.
- Rotation also forced per-category accounting: the payload used to carry one
  shared `perCategory` remainder, and with one category per slice the category
  that ran spent the other one's count, so both would stop near half the target.
  The payload now carries `remaining` per category, only the category that ran
  is charged, an exhausted category is zeroed, and a category owed less than the
  slice is capped instead of overshooting.
- A category that threw before searching keeps its whole count and is retried on
  a delay, but only when the failure can succeed later. `supplierSourcingErrorCode`
  reads the reason by shape, so `discovery_unavailable` and unexpected errors are
  retryable while `not_found` and `unsupported_category` end the wave instead of
  burning three futile delayed slices.
- Verification: `npm run test:procurement-sourcing-command`,
  `npm run test:procurement-sourcing-wave`, `npx tsc --noEmit` (only the
  pre-existing `dashboard/admin/page.tsx` route typing error).

- Added chat threads to the company context without a schema change: threads
  are `CompanyContext` rows of kind `CHAT_THREAD`, message payloads carry

  `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out.
- Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` (only pre-existing

## 2026-08-29: A queued sourcing wave stopped after one slice

- Production symptom: the 100 per category wave queued, the first slice ran, and
  then no job was ever due again. Repeated drains returned
  `{"scanned":0}`, while the direct run showed `examined: 12`, `added: 1`,
  `discoveryExhausted: true`, `queriesUsed` of length one.
- Cause: every slice started at query round 0, so it searched the same phrase the
  earlier slice had searched. Discovery excludes known domains, the search
  returned nothing new, the wave set `discoveryExhausted` on that first barren
  round, and the continuation condition read that as a category with nothing left
  to find.
- Fix: the wave takes `startRound` and returns `nextRound`, the queued job stores
  a per category `startRounds` cursor, a barren round moves to the next phrases
  (up to 3 in a row) instead of ending the wave, and a category is exhausted only
  once `supplierSourcingQueryRounds` are spent. A slice with phrases left keeps
  the chain alive; an outage retry replays the phrases it never searched.
- Verification: `npm run test:procurement-sourcing-wave`,
  `npm run test:procurement-sourcing-command`, `npx tsc --noEmit` (only the
  pre-existing typed route error on `src/app/dashboard/admin/page.tsx`).

## 2026-08-28: A discovery call gets enough time to answer

- Production symptom: every drained sourcing slice completed and added nobody,
  with `providerFailures: ["openai-web-search", "openai-web-search"]`,
  `examined: 0`, `timedOut: true`.
- Cause: `MAX_DISCOVERY_CALL_MS` was 60s while one high context web search takes
  roughly 60 to 100s, and `runSourcingCommand` split the 120s slice budget evenly
  across the planned categories, so each discovery call was abandoned before it
  could answer.
- `MAX_DISCOVERY_CALL_MS` is 130s, `SOURCING_COMMAND_SLICE_BUDGET_MS` is 230s,
  the OpenAI discovery client makes one attempt with a 110s timeout instead of
  retrying, and a category is handed the whole remaining budget. A later category
  that no longer has room for one discovery call is left to the continuation
  slice, while the first category always runs.

## 2026-08-28: Bounded follow ups for quiet suppliers

- Added `src/lib/procurement-supplier-chase.ts` (pure quiet thread policy) and a

- `src/lib/procurement-file-delivery-draft.ts` stores a draft `variant`, and the

- `src/lib/procurement-reply-send.ts` gained `requireQuietThread`, which anchors

  idempotency scope.

## 2026-08-25: Draft tasks stay PLANNED, attachment bytes load after the claim

- `src/lib/procurement-file-delivery-draft.ts` inserted the draft task as
  `READY`, which the execution trigger rejects, so the "Draft with request files"
  action returned a server error in the browser. The task is now created as
  `PLANNED`, a redraft cancels any prior live draft and writes a new versioned
  task key, and the draft read looks for the latest `PLANNED` task.
- `src/lib/procurement-reply-send.ts` split attachment handling: identity and the
  message hash come from the request itself without touching storage, and bytes
  are loaded and screened only on the fresh send path, after the claim. The
  loader is injectable so the ordering is testable.
- Added `scripts/procurement-file-draft-database.test.ts` (trigger lifecycle,
  withheld sensitive file, reload, redraft supersession, office scope) and an
  unresolved send scenario in `scripts/procurement-reply-send-database.test.ts`
  that reconciles while document storage fails. Both run in CI now.
- Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `next lint` on the changed files,
  `npm run test:supplier-attachment-drafts`, `npm run test:procurement-reply-route`,
  `npm run test:procurement-reply-draft`, and both database contracts against a
  migrated disposable database. No supplier mail was sent.

- Added `src/lib/procurement-file-delivery-draft.ts` which saves a durable

## Log

### 2026-08-22 - Move customers into the company-scoped full app

- Branch: `customer-full-app-access-clean-20260822`, based on current main.
- Task: Replace the separate customer summary as the primary experience with
  the real Supply OS, while preserving strict company scope and removing admin
  settings from customer sessions.
- Data model: Added unique customer usernames, encrypted administrator-readable
  passwords, linked app identities, and Supply workspace memberships.
- Security: Customer sessions are revalidated against active portal and
  workspace memberships. Customer API access is restricted to assigned
  workspaces, admin mutations stay blocked, and connector management is denied.
- Migration: Existing accounts are backfilled from company names. A populated
  HypnoDreamz fixture migrated to username `hypnodreamz`, a linked restricted
  app identity, and active editor workspace access.
- Verification: Focused auth and procurement contracts, database tests under
  the restricted app role, full migration chain and repeat deploy, populated
  backfill, Prisma validation, TypeScript, product copy, and production build.
- Caveat: An admin must set a password after migration before an existing
  account can sign in. Rotating `AUTH_SECRET` makes saved readable passwords
  unavailable and requires an admin reset.

### 2026-08-20 - Repair unified Neon schema and remove implicit Atlas fallback

- Branch: `fix/remove-implicit-atlas-fallback`, based on production main.
- Task: Keep production on the current Neon database, restore the missing app
  schema, and stop unresolved workspace state from rendering Atlas Robotics.
- Root cause: The production migration ledger marked all 27 migrations as
  applied even though 82 quoted Prisma tables were absent. The live
  `/api/supply-os/workspaces` route failed on the missing `SupplyWorkspace`
  relation. Atlas was a client demo fallback, not a second database.
- Database work: Captured a local custom-format backup, rehearsed the additive
  schema repair inside a rollback transaction, then created only missing Prisma
  tables, indexes, foreign keys, domain checks, and tenant-scope triggers. The
  lowercase workflow tables were retained. Restored `derya_app` grants and
  created the active HypnoDreamz workspace and OWNER membership.
- Application work: Removed the automatic Atlas identity and inventory fallback
  from normal loading. Presentation mode requests Atlas explicitly.
- Verification: Prisma migration status, rollback rehearsal, restricted-role
  grant checks, HypnoDreamz workspace query, company navigation contract,
  TypeScript, production build, diff hygiene, and forbidden-character scan.
- Caveat: The backup is local to the controlled workstation and should not be
  treated as the long-term Neon backup policy.

### 2026-08-20 - Collapse Context to CompanyDocument and repair uploads

- Branch: `fix/minimal-company-context-v2`, based on production main.
- Task: Remove the six-table Context backend and fix the production upload path
  without changing the approved single-chat product surface.
- Root cause: `storeContextDocumentFile` selected local storage in production,
  and Vercel rejected the write before extraction or persistence. Every file
  type therefore returned the same generic 500 response.
- Files above 3 MB are uploaded in bounded chunks so the 10 MB product limit
  does not hit Vercel's 4.5 MB function request limit. Chunks use the existing
  `CompanyDocument` table and are deleted after assembly or expiry.
- Original-file downloads use a 64 KB `ReadableStream` so the response path
  remains valid for files above the platform's buffered response limit.
- Files changed: Prisma schema and migration, company document ingestion,
  Context agent and authenticated routes, internal chat, portal removal,
  canonical memory taxonomy, app-role allowlist, focused tests, and release
  documentation.
- Safety: Reads and writes resolve the authenticated office, accessible supply
  workspace, and linked company on the server. Uploaded content is untrusted,
  and the agent has no outbound side effects.
- Verification: Prisma validation, document and Context contracts, customer
  isolation, product copy, deployment boundary, TypeScript, production build,
  migration CI, and live authenticated upload are the release gates.
- Caveat: This sandbox cannot start disposable PostgreSQL because System V
  shared memory is blocked. GitHub PostgreSQL CI must execute the full migration
  and database-backed Context contract before merge.

  `CRON_SECRET` to match production. Historical counts will rise progressively

### 2026-07-04 - Persistent sessions until explicit logout

- Branch: crm-v1-review-and-push (pushed to main)
- Task: Session cookie maxAge raised from 7 days to 400 days (SESSION_MAX_AGE
  in src/lib/auth.ts), the longest lifetime browsers honor per the cookie
  spec, so sign-in persists across restarts until the user hits Log out.
  Session is a stateless HMAC cookie with no server-side expiry, so maxAge is
  the sole lifetime control.
- Files changed: src/lib/auth.ts.
- Verification: tsc clean, build ok. No migration.
- Caveats: takes effect on next sign-in; existing 7-day cookies keep their
  old expiry until re-login. No server-side revocation (logout clears the
  cookie locally, as before).

  freed space flowed back into the flex Subject column, shifting columns the

### 2026-08-07 - Fix production Supply OS stream cutoff

- Branch: hotfix-supply-research-terminal, targeting main
- Symptom: the AON3D example emitted only `Searching public sources`, then the
  browser reported that research ended without a dashboard result.

  slower public-search call first. The production function ended while waiting
  on that upstream call, outside the route's normal result and error events.

  valid public website. Retain public search as recovery if the official site is
  unreachable, and cap name-only model calls at 20 seconds with zero SDK
  retries.

  name-only configured, and unavailable cases.

  returned the official name, website, four sources, and six progress events in
  1.6 seconds.

### 2026-08-07 - Make name-only company research terminal and correct

- Branch: `fix/supply-os-research-quality`, targeting `main`
- Commits: `de33b50`, `eb85d15`, `dc7e9e4`, `fa62a03`
- Symptom: `do nox metals` emitted early progress, then production ended the
  stream without a dashboard.
- Root cause: name-only prompts still made provider-backed public search the
  prerequisite for the first usable result. A host cutoff could therefore
  occur outside the route's result and error handling.
- Research fix: generate likely domains from the company name, inspect each
  with bounded SSRF-safe official-site requests, score identity evidence,
  reject parked or mismatched domains, and keep model search as optional

### 2026-08-12 - Move supplier research to durable queued work

- Branch: `codex/supplier-campaign-local`, integration worktree targeting the
  current main branch.
- Root cause: the supplier-research POST owned the provider call. The host could
  terminate that request while the client remained in a local running state,
  leaving the operator with zero sources and no durable progress to resume.
- Runtime: the route now returns HTTP 202 after persisting or reusing the run.
  The exact-run GET polls the durable record. `after()` provides a fast start;
  the protected cron advances campaigns, runs at most two workers, then
  reconciles campaign state. Claims are atomic, queued work is not stale-failed,
  and worker failures are sanitized before persistence.
- UI: the procurement workspace polls QUEUED and RUNNING status, renders saved
  terminal output, and moves long work to a clear background state after three
  minutes without cancelling it.
- Campaign: the existing run table also stores the fixed GUILD parent, child
  attempts, and aggregate results without a schema change. Thirty-eight lines
  search for three to five distinct attributable leads. GUILD-027 remains a
  quantity and unit clarification. GUILD-039 is an award documentation
  requirement. Batches, retry backoff, attempt ceilings, and daily campaign and
  office caps prevent perpetual HTTP and unbounded provider work.
- Provenance and retry: parents and aggregate artifacts now use the enforced
  QUEUED to RUNNING to terminal transitions. Retrying a failed campaign creates
  a linked immutable generation, and reconciliation reads validated aggregate
  and attempt history across that bounded lineage. Aggregate artifacts are not
  charged as provider calls. Manual retry is capped at twelve generations and
  ancestry reads reject overflow instead of silently truncating it.
- Concurrency hardening: an expiring token on the RUNNING parent fences every
  aggregate write, child enqueue, lease release, and terminal transition under
  a parent row lock. Aggregate revisions carry attempt watermarks across retry
  generations. Older work cannot overwrite newer evidence, while current
  receipt validation can persist a smaller or empty corrected aggregate.
- Quota hardening: campaign reservation and provider claim share an
  office-stable advisory lock. The UTC quota day and persisted timestamps are
  derived from `clock_timestamp()` after that lock is acquired, closing the
  midnight rollover race in the 72-call daily office bound.
- Provider and evidence boundary: campaign child work requires Exa forced-live
  validation, so a configuration change cannot silently switch it to the
  source-only OpenAI path. Generic product or material pages must also support
  distinguishing request qualifiers, including requested material grade and a
  critical dimension when present, before they count toward the lead target.
- Acceptance: the single-run deployed check now requires an explicit base URL,
  authenticated cookie, and workspace ID, expects HTTP 202, and polls the exact
  run to a terminal state. The new campaign check resumes the fixed campaign and
  requires 38 completed searchable lines with three to five attributable
  `REVIEW_REQUIRED` candidates in each aggregate run plus the explicit 027 and
  039 states.
- CI registration: worker lifecycle, client polling, retained supplier lead,
  deterministic continuous campaign, and Atlas sourcing tests now run in the
  Supply OS workflow. Server-only lifecycle execution uses the React server
  condition. Atlas uses `node --import tsx` to avoid the restricted `tsx` IPC
  path.
- Focused checks passed: `test:supply-os-bom-acceptance`,
  `test:supply-os-research-worker-lifecycle`,
  `test:supply-os-supplier-research-polling`,
  `test:supply-os-supplier-leads`, and `test:supply-os-atlas-sourcing`.
- Integration checks passed: deterministic continuous campaign, supplier lead,
  route lifecycle, worker lifecycle, polling, Atlas, BOM, Exa retrieval,
  sourcing projection, ingestion trust, product copy, TypeScript, and the
  production build. PostgreSQL-backed persistence remains delegated to CI

  workspace ID, or provider credentials were available. Before release, run the

  and never included in memory events. Password, status, and access changes
  increment the session version so old sessions are rejected. Five failed

  throttle rows through the expiry index.

  Customer management can generate, show, copy, and set a password,

  runner records the exact outbound plan before SMTP. Each delivery has a

### 2026-08-25 - Locale-aware document lead generation

  that key.

  and comma, tab, or semicolon data. Rows retain source URL and row index and
  deduplicate by domain or normalized company name. Names-only rows are kept
  with `needsResolution`, while sparse PDF marketing material is discarded.
- Added offline fixtures for query locales, Serper filtering, repeated PDF
  headers and footers, non-English table headers, and semicolon data.

### 2026-08-25 - Expand document hits into research rows

  existing office-scoped research list path, including names-only rows marked
  for resolution and document provenance in the existing `buys` field.
- Directory classification now applies row-count and density checks to every
  supported document kind. Layout tables fall back to single-company harvest,
  and caller-provided regions are escaped before city matching.
- Added offline coverage for same-host documents, layout-table fallback,
  metacharacter regions, multiple inline emails, and directory persistence.

### 2026-08-25 - Bound directory verification work

  company names when source formatting differs from normalized contact output.
- Directory email verification checks the batch deadline before each row, so
  completed rows remain available without allowing a large document to overrun
  its bounded run.

### 2026-08-25 - Preserve non-Latin directory names

  distinct domainless Cyrillic, Arabic, or CJK names from collapsing together.

  hostname, URL, and network parsing; company-name and header normalization
  now use Unicode-aware classes.

### 2026-08-25 - Keep HTML directory row provenance monotonic

- HTML table parsing now assigns row indexes from one page-level data-row
  counter, preventing duplicate provenance numbers across multiple tables.

### 2026-08-26 - Keep the first row of headerless delimited directories

- Delimited parsing skips the first line only when a header field is
  recognized, so a CSV or TSV that starts with data keeps its first company.
- The directory-density denominator follows the same decision, so headerless
  documents are no longer measured against a phantom header line.

  workspace recorded on the request, scoped to the office and company that own
  it. Existing citations are never rewritten and reruns add nothing.

### 2026-08-26 - Scope a sourcing request to the files it should send

  that set, and reports what it removed. Omitting names keeps the additive
  behavior.

### 2026-08-28 - A sourcing slice fits inside one invocation

- Capped every external call inside the supplier sourcing wave (discovery,
  crawl, email verification) and clamped each cap to the wave deadline, because
  a single 90s web search with a retry outlasted the whole slice budget and the
  drained invocation was killed at 300s with no response.
- Cut the slice to 10 suppliers and 120s of sourcing so the remainder of the
  invocation covers the RFQ sends and the continuation enqueue.
- `runDueBackgroundJobs` now reclaims jobs stuck `RUNNING` for 15 minutes, up to
  five attempts, so a job killed mid invocation stops holding its dedupe key.

### 2026-08-31 - A sourcing wave survives a supplier that will not save

- `insertSourcedVendor` was the one uncaught call inside the wave, so a single
  rejected row, for example an exhausted Prisma connection pool, threw away the
  whole slice including the suppliers already qualified and the RFQ sends they
  had earned. The write now fails only that supplier, recorded as a rejection
  with its reason.
- An unexpected wave failure keeps a short reason. `failureReason` clips it to
  one line, the operator command reports it as `errorReason` next to the same
  opaque message, and the queued continuation carries it as `lastFailure` so the
  status endpoint explains an unattended wave that keeps failing.

### 2026-08-31 - A sourcing wave tells a broken database from a bad row

- `failureReason` now reports a fixed class ("the database connection failed",
  "the database rejected the row") instead of the driver message, so no schema,
  host, or role detail reaches an API result, a queued payload, or a log line.
- A save failure that is about the shared database stops the slice, is reported
  as `persistenceFailures`, and leaves `nextRound` where the slice started. The
  queued job treats that as an outage: the count and the search cursor survive
  and the work is retried, rather than turning qualified suppliers into
  rejections while the continuation spends fresh phrases. A row level failure
  (value too long, duplicate) stays a per-supplier rejection.
- The reason a chain stops is written onto the finished job payload, and the
  status reads the last finished job when nothing is queued, so a wave that
  ended on a failure still explains itself.

### 2026-08-31 - Procurement research cron drains queued runs

- The procurement research cron now runs the enqueue backstop first and then
  drains queued supplier research with the existing lease and stale-run
  handling.
- Each phase has an independent error boundary. Previously queued work still
  drains after an enqueue failure, while both failures produce the only 503
  response. Partial failures remain 200 responses with explicit error markers.
- The worker limit remains capped at two, and the legacy supplier research cron
  remains untouched.

### 2026-08-31 - Sourcing surfaces state what they know

- The customer procurement request detail tracks its own fetch: the first load
  is deduplicated per abort signal, an aborted or failed load renders "Supplier
  results did not load" with a retry and a way back to the queue, and supplier
  counts stay hidden until an authoritative detail arrives instead of rendering
  zeros. Polling now covers the approval statuses, so a request waiting for a
  shortlist decision keeps refreshing.
- Pending shortlist and order approvals are announced on the queue row action
  ("Review shortlist", "Review order") and above the Messages supplier table,
  not only inside the request detail.
- Vendor contact and reply reads reconcile the workflow receipt with the
  connected email thread, so a vendor with thread traffic and no workflow
  receipt reads as "N messages in the connected thread, no workflow receipt
  saved" instead of contradicting the Messages tab.
- Context prospecting cards report "Searches run", "Pages read", "Companies
  found", and "N of M rows saved", keep Dismiss reachable while a run is
  tracked, and treat a run with no progress past the stale threshold as
  interrupted so it can be retried.
- Chat threads are renamed from the first operator message, clarifying-question
  answers are keyed by message id so an older question keeps its own state, the
  inferred facility objects link to the verification surface, long material and
  company names carry native titles, and loading is separated from failure on
  the company profile and company index.

  cue is the one that cue labels. `mergeSupplierQuoteReadings` folds a thread of
  inbound readings newest first.
- `procurement-supplier-quote.ts`: candidates read the whole inbound thread, and
  an already recorded supplier is listed without a read so the run budget stays
  available for suppliers that still need capture.

### 2026-09-02 - Operator office mail surface

- Campaign and demo outbound persistence now invokes the existing
  `logEmailTouch` resolver after the local transaction or message write.
- Added office-scoped Mail thread and detail reads with deterministic keyset
  pagination, participant parsing, company and contact links, and pooled
  mailbox attribution from the newest outbound message.
- Added an operator-only Supply OS Mail tab. Customer and employee contexts
  are hidden in the shell and rejected again in the backend.
- Mail detail renders only stored body text and treats missing body text as an
  empty body.

## 2026-09-02: Supplier state, facility verification, and shortlist counts

- The request detail Compare table showed the raw workflow vendor status, so a
  vendor could read "contacted" there while the Messages tab reported no
  receipt. Both surfaces now derive the supplier line from receipts:
  `customerProcurementVendorStateLabel` reads quote, response count, and
  contact receipt in that order.
- A saved operating base is operator-entered, so the map inspector no longer
  asks to verify the company operating site when it matches that base. Matching
  is limited to the factory object through `facilityMatchesVerifiedBase`, so
  other facilities in the same city stay unverified.
- `awaiting_shortlist_approval` progress no longer claims "0 supplier
  candidates" when the caller has no candidate count, which is the case for the
  queue projection.

## 2026-09-02: Supplier quote reading, denominators, questions, and durations

- A unit price needs a unit denominator. `UNIT_PRICE_CUE` allowed the noun after
  `per` to be absent, so "$100 per order" and "$400 per shipment" priced the
  whole job yet read as a price per piece. `per` and the slash form now require
  an accepted unit noun, while standalone "each" and "apiece" still count.
- A question states nothing, so the interrogative guard runs before any fact is
  read: "can you accept delivery in three weeks?" no longer sets a lead time,
  MOQ, or quantity. A non-question disclaimer keeps its old scope, suppressing
  the amounts beside it while leaving a lead time the supplier stated.
- A duration a supplier attaches to a warranty, a price validity, payment
  terms, or storage is not a delivery promise, so `NON_DELIVERY_DURATION`
  rejects the clause: "delivery includes a 12 month warranty" is not a 360 day
  lead time. "Delivery in 3 weeks" and "lead time is 20 days" are unchanged.
- One autopilot pass now sweeps quote capture with its own cursor across
  bounded pages, so a request whose first page of respondents stays unquoted
  cannot hide the priced replies behind them from every later pass. A failed
  write ends the sweep, because the cursor rewound to that retry.

## 2026-09-03: Retractions, cost breakdowns, and currency words in quote reading

- A refusal reaches back over the whole message, not only over older messages. A
  supplier who writes "our price is $10 each, lead time 3 weeks, we cannot honor
  that price" leaves no price standing, so the reading drops the earlier amount
  when the retraction is read, while a replacement written after the refusal is
  read normally and stands.
- Question detection is shared with triage through `supplierQuestionSentence`,
  so an interrogative without a question mark ("would 20 days delivery work for
  you") states no lead time either.
- One line of a cost breakdown is not the order total. "PCB cost is 132usd,
  assembly cost is 456usd, components cost is 3520usd" priced the order at 132
  before, which would have made a request purchase ready for a fraction of its
  cost, so a bare lot price is only read when a single clause in the sentence
  carries a priced amount.
- A currency code is a whole word: the "TL" inside "STL 2" no longer prices two
  Turkish lira, which is what a molder's file list read as before.

## 2026-08-31: Send time state recheck for supplier file replies

- Before this change the only server side stale state refusals lived in the
  procurement approval and purchase order paths. A supplier file bearing draft
  showed a stale badge in the dashboard, but the send path itself accepted a
  draft written from request state that had since changed.
- `procurement-file-draft-freshness.ts` hashes the request fields and file
  identity a reply actually repeats to the supplier: material, normalized
  quantity, unit, needed by date, specification, request document ids, names,
  summaries and content hashes, and attachment ids, names, mime types, and
  sizes. Documents and attachments are sorted by document id, so hashing is
  order independent.
- The fingerprint is written into the planned execution task input at draft
  time and restored on read, which keeps it under the existing immutability
  trigger instead of adding a mutable column.
- The recheck fails closed. An unreadable request state refuses the delivery
  the same way a changed one does, and a draft saved before this change has no
  fingerprint, so it is refused with its own reason until it is redrafted.
- Refusals are durable: the run summary counts them and the supplier
  communication event trail records the stored and current fingerprint.
- Review follow up: the fingerprint now covers only supplier visible content
  (attached documents and the field lines the reply body renders), the delivery
  batch rereads the request per draft so a mid run edit is caught, and a refusal
  whose event trail write failed says so in its reason instead of reading like a
  routine stale outcome.
- The suite now asserts the unaudited case directly: a refusal whose draft task
  is no longer planned must refuse, report `audited: false`, and name the missing
  trail entry in its reason.
- `renderedDocumentContext` is now the one reader of document lines for both the
  reply body and the fingerprint, so a field line past the body's shared
  character budget is not treated as supplier visible state. The suite controls
  for it with a document whose fields run past the per document line budget.

## 2026-09-02: Feast leadgen profile and office

- Added the Feast profile and provisioned the Feast office via
  `POST /api/ops/offices` for a South of England coffee shop and cafe campaign.
- The mailing list is to be imported as a research list via
  `POST /api/ops/research/import` with list slug `feast-south-england-cafes`,
  then reviewed before any outreach.

## 2026-09-03: Supplier reply reachability diagnostics, review follow ups

- `procurementInboxDiagnostics` pages the tagged message scan instead of taking
  one capped slice and reports `truncated` when the ceiling bites, so a large
  campaign's mailbox, supplier and stranded counts are whole rather than silently
  partial.
- An inbound message whose mailbox row was deleted is attributed to the mailbox
  its thread was sent from, so a supplier address is never reported as one of our
  mailboxes; an inbound message with no resolvable mailbox is bucketed instead.
- A stranded reply with no subject at all now counts as stranded, since a SQL
  null dropped out of the `NOT contains` comparison entirely.
- `strandedSample` names the most recent stranded replies (sender, subject, time)
  so an operator can tell a supplier answer that lost the RFQ tag from unrelated
  mail on the same thread.
- Production run on both HypnoDreamz requests: all 21 pool mailboxes ingest and
  are fresh, 0 suppliers written to from an unreachable mailbox, but 22 (PCBA)
  and 19 (foam) ingested inbound replies sit on our own RFQ threads without the
  reference in the subject, so the request never counts them.

## 2026-09-03: Leadgen exclusions and balanced plans

- Draft-derived leadgen profiles now skip region-less query plans when regions
  are provided.
- Added optional `hardExclusions` to leadgen profiles. Feast chain names now
  reject a lead only when they appear in its company name or domain, while
  mentions in page text remain allowed.
- Limited query plans are now interleaved across keywords, regions, segments,
  locales, and shapes so bounded runs retain broad coverage.
- Query plan ordering is versioned, so legacy prospecting actions restart from
  offset zero while actions created with the current plan version resume safely.
- Directory prospecting now drops hard-rejected rows before email verification or candidate accounting.

## 2026-09-04: Conversation task transitions are atomic and backoff covers every retry

- A conversation task transition now reads and writes its row inside one
  transaction holding a row lock, so two overlapping passes that both fail on
  the same supplier both increment the attempt count instead of one silently
  overwriting the other. A create that loses the unique key race retries once.
- Per conversation backoff is read before the quote sweep and the draft batch,
  not only before the funnel scan, and the backing off supplier ids are passed
  into both. A quote write or draft that keeps failing is left alone until its
  own next attempt is due, while a request stays in the queue for its other
  suppliers.
- Coverage: a database concurrency regression for the two overlapping failures,
  and wiring assertions that the lock, the create race retry, and the backoff
  handoff into the quote and draft paths are all in place.
- The scheduled pass now intersects the due conversation read with the queue it
  may work, in the database, before the limit. A request that reached an order
  or was cancelled keeps its unsettled tasks, and those are the oldest due rows,
  so limiting first could fill the whole result with requests the pass then
  discarded and leave a live failing request unled.

## 2026-09-04: A paused thread mailbox is not an empty sender pool

- A reservation pinned to one mailbox (a reply or follow up has to leave from
  the mailbox that owns the supplier's thread) applied the shared sender pool
  filter, so a mailbox paused by sender protection produced no candidate row and
  the failure read "No connected email account is enabled in the sender pool".
  Production showed that message while the pool held four connected mailboxes,
  which points an operator at connecting mailboxes instead of resuming the
  paused one.
- `reserveEmailSender` now answers `SENDER_UNAVAILABLE` for a pinned mailbox and
  names the actual condition: paused (with the pause reason), sending turned
  off, disabled, disconnected, or gone. `POOL_EMPTY` again means only that the
  shared pool has no connected sender.
- Every caller treats `SENDER_UNAVAILABLE` like a capacity shortage rather than
  a refusal, since a paused mailbox can be resumed: supplier nudges and bulk RFQ
  count it as exhausted capacity and retry the supplier, and campaign send and
  follow ups defer the recipient instead of settling it as rejected.
- The read-only inbox diagnostic now reports how many connected mailboxes sender
  protection holds out of the pool, with each pause reason and time, plus the
  pause reason on each of the request's own blocked mailboxes.
- Coverage: a database regression reserving against a paused pinned mailbox
  asserts the code and the reason text, pure assertions cover every reason
  branch, and source contracts assert each caller defers rather than refuses.
